textArabic: الْمُسْلِمُ مَنْ سَلِمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِهِ وَيَدِهِ
textEnglish: The true Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hands other people are completely safe.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 10, Sahih Muslim 40 · Chapter 60: Zakat al-Fitr before Eid Prayer
keyLesson: Righteousness is verified when those around you live in safety from your harm and speech.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: What spiritual wisdom did the Prophet ﷺ teach regarding smiling and pleasant words as charity?
textArabic: إِنَّمَا الأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ، وَإِنَّمَا لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى
textEnglish: Actions are judged by motives and intentions, and every person will have only that which they intended.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1, Sahih Muslim 1907 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Purify your heart before every deed; a sincere intention transforms simple daily acts into perpetual worship.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: What divine wisdom did the Prophet ﷺ reveal regarding smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الإِيمَانُ أَنْ تُؤْمِنَ بِاللَّهِ، وَمَلاَئِكَتِهِ، وَكُتُبِهِ، وَرُسُلِهِ، وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ، وَتُؤْمِنَ بِالْقَدَرِ خَيْرِهِ وَشَرِّهِ
textEnglish: Faith is that you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and divine destiny—both its prosperity and adversity.
reference: Sahih Muslim 8 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Conviction in Allah’s wisdom gives the believer unwavering calm during life’s unpredictable changes.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: How does consistent practice of smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الرَّاحِمُونَ يَرْحَمُهُمُ الرَّحْمَنُ، ارْحَمُوا مَنْ فِي الأَرْضِ يَرْحَمْكُمْ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاءِ
textEnglish: The merciful will be shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Be merciful to those on earth, and the One in the heavens will be merciful to you.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1924, Sunan Abi Dawud 4941 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Compassion to all living beings is the golden key that unlocks divine mercy and forgiveness.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: What spiritual remedy does smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لاَ يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لأَخِيهِ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ
textEnglish: None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 13, Sahih Muslim 45 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Genuine faith cleanses the soul of jealousy and cultivates sincere goodwill toward all people.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: Why is sincere commitment to smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّ مِنْ خِيَارِكُمْ أَحْسَنَكُمْ أَخْلاَقًا
textEnglish: Indeed, the best and most beloved among you are those who possess the best character and manners.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 3559, Sahih Muslim 2321 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Gentleness, integrity, and warmth of character are the true reflection of a living faith.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: How did the noble Companions embody smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الطُّهُورُ شَطْرُ الإِيمَانِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ تَمْلأُ الْمِيزَانَ
textEnglish: Purity is half of faith, and “Alhamdulillah” (Praise be to Allah) fills the divine scale of deeds.
reference: Sahih Muslim 223 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Inner and outer purification are intertwined; heartfelt gratitude tilts the eternal scale in your favor.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: What warning or glad tiding is conveyed concerning smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: أَوَّلُ مَا يُحَاسَبُ بِهِ الْعَبْدُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ مِنْ عَمَلِهِ صَلاَتُهُ
textEnglish: The first matter for which the slave of Allah will be brought to account on the Day of Judgment is his prayer.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 413, Sunan an-Nasa’i 465 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Salah is your personal appointment with the Lord of the worlds; safeguard its punctuality and focus.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: In what way does excellence in smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّ الدِّينَ يُسْرٌ، وَلَنْ يُشَادَّ الدِّينَ أَحَدٌ إِلاَّ غَلَبَهُ
textEnglish: Indeed, the religion is easy, and no one makes the religion overly difficult except that it will overcome him.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 39 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Adopt a steady, balanced pace of devotion; moderation sustains lifelong spiritual growth.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: How can one safeguard smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لَيْسَ الْغِنَى عَنْ كَثْرَةِ الْعَرَضِ، وَلَكِنَّ الْغِنَى غِنَى النَّفْسِ
textEnglish: Richness is not about abundance of worldly possessions; true wealth is the richness of contentment in the soul.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6446, Sahih Muslim 1051 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Peace is never found in endless material craving, but in tranquility and satisfaction with what Allah gave.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: What essential principle transforms our approach to smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ فَلْيَقُلْ خَيْرًا أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ
textEnglish: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak what is beneficial or remain silent.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6018, Sahih Muslim 47 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Guarding speech protects relationships and preserves the dignity and purity of the heart.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: Why is genuine devotion in smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَثَلُ الَّذِي يَذْكُرُ رَبَّهُ وَالَّذِي لاَ يَذْكُرُ رَبَّهُ مَثَلُ الْحَيِّ وَالْمَيِّتِ
textEnglish: The example of the one who remembers his Lord compared to the one who does not is like that of the living and the dead.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6407, Sahih Muslim 779 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Dhikr is the oxygen of the spiritual heart; without it, the inner being withers.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: How does the heart find tranquility through smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَا يُصِيبُ الْمُسْلِمَ مِنْ نَصَبٍ وَلاَ وَصَبٍ وَلاَ هَمٍّ وَلاَ حَزَنٍ وَلاَ أَذًى حَتَّى الشَّوْكَةِ يُشَاكُهَا إِلاَّ كَفَّرَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مِنْ خَطَايَاهُ
textEnglish: No fatigue, illness, worry, grief, hurt, or distress befalls a believer—even the prick of a thorn—except that Allah expiates some of his sins through it.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5641, Sahih Muslim 2573 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Every silent patience during hardship is recognized, rewarded, and purified by the Most Merciful.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: What common pitfall did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ warn about in smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: تَبَسُّمُكَ فِي وَجْهِ أَخِيكَ لَكَ صَدَقَةٌ
textEnglish: Your smiling in the face of your brother is charity for you.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1956 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Radiating warmth and gentle kindness costs nothing yet carries eternal divine reward.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: How does moral beauty manifest through smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الْمُسْلِمُ مَنْ سَلِمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِهِ وَيَدِهِ
textEnglish: The true Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hands other people are completely safe.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 10, Sahih Muslim 40 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Righteousness is verified when those around you live in safety from your harm and speech.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: What eternal reward is promised for cultivating smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
textEnglish: The best among you are those who learn the Quran and teach it to others.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5027 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Connecting yourself with the Book of Allah and sharing its light with others is the pinnacle of nobility.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: How can parents and mentors inspire smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ سَلَكَ طَرِيقًا يَلْتَمِسُ فِيهِ عِلْمًا سَهَّلَ اللَّهُ لَهُ بِهِ طَرِيقًا إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ
textEnglish: Whoever travels a path seeking sacred knowledge, Allah makes smooth for him a path to Paradise.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2699 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Every moment dedicated to understanding faith and truth brings you closer to the gardens of Jannah.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: What guidance did the Prophet ﷺ emphasize regarding consistency in smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لاَ تَغْضَبْ، فَرَدَّدَ مِرَارًا، قَالَ: لاَ تَغْضَبْ
textEnglish: A man said to the Prophet: “Advise me.” He said: “Do not become angry.” The man repeated his request several times, and each time he replied: “Do not become angry.”
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6116 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Mastery over impulsive anger preserves wisdom, protects relationships, and prevents regret.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: How does divine mercy embrace those who strive in smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: اتَّقِ اللَّهَ حَيْثُمَا كُنْتَ، وَأَتْبِعِ السَّيِّئَةَ الْحَسَنَةَ تَمْحُهَا، وَخَالِقِ النَّاسَ بِخُلُقٍ حَسَنٍ
textEnglish: Be mindful of Allah wherever you are; follow an evil deed with a good one and it will erase it; and treat people with beautiful character.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1987 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Live with God-consciousness in private and public, rapidly correct missteps, and be gracious to all.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: In times of difficulty, how does smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: كُلُّكُمْ رَاعٍ وَكُلُّكُمْ مَسْئُولٌ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهِ
textEnglish: Every one of you is a shepherd and guardian, and every one of you will be questioned concerning his flock.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 893, Sahih Muslim 1829 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Leadership is a sacred trust and responsibility of service, not privilege or authority.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: What reflection on the Hereafter is awakened by smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ إِذَا عَمِلَ أَحَدُكُمْ عَمَلاً أَنْ يُتْقِنَهُ
textEnglish: Verily, Allah loves that whenever any of you undertakes a work, he executes it with mastery and excellence (Itqan).
reference: Shu’ab al-Iman (Al-Bayhaqi 4929, Hasan) · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Excellence in profession, study, and daily duty is an act of devotion loved by the Creator.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: How does understanding smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الْحَيَاءُ لاَ يَأْتِي إِلاَّ بِخَيْرٍ
textEnglish: Modesty and conscience (Haya) bring nothing except goodness.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6117, Sahih Muslim 37 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Haya is a spiritual shield that restrains the soul from vulgarity and prompts noble conduct.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: What divine wisdom did the Prophet ﷺ reveal regarding smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ كَفَلَ يَتِيمًا لَهُ أَوْ لِغَيْرِهِ فَأَنَا وَهُوَ كَهَاتَيْنِ فِي الْجَنَّةِ
textEnglish: The one who cares for an orphan and myself will be together in Paradise like these two fingers (joining his index and middle finger).
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5304, Sahih Muslim 2983 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Caring for vulnerable orphans guarantees the closest companionship with the Prophet ﷺ in the highest Jannah.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: How does consistent practice of smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَا نَقَصَتْ صَدَقَةٌ مِنْ مَالٍ، وَمَا زَادَ اللَّهُ عَبْدًا بِعَفْوٍ إِلاَّ عِزًّا
textEnglish: Charity never decreases wealth; and Allah never increases a servant who forgives except in honor and elevation.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2588 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Generosity and forgiveness never degrade a person; they invoke divine barakah and nobility.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: What spiritual remedy does smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: احْفَظِ اللَّهَ يَحْفَظْكَ، احْفَظِ اللَّهَ تَجِدْهُ تُجَاهَكَ
textEnglish: Be mindful of Allah, and He will protect you. Be mindful of Allah, and you will find Him facing you in every need.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2516 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Honor Allah’s commands in times of ease, and He will deliver and comfort you in times of adversity.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: Why is sincere commitment to smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لَوْ أَنَّكُمْ تَوَكَّلُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ حَقَّ تَوَكُّلِهِ لَرَزَقَكُمْ كَمَا يَرْزُقُ الطَّيْرَ
textEnglish: If you were to rely upon Allah with true reliance (Tawakkul), He would provide for you just as He provides for birds: they depart hungry at dawn and return full at dusk.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2344, Sunan Ibn Majah 4164 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Combine practical effort with tranquil reliance upon the Ultimate Provider.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: How did the noble Companions embody smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: أَفْشُوا السَّلاَمَ، وَأَطْعِمُوا الطَّعَامَ، وَصِلُوا الأَرْحَامَ، وَصَلُّوا بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّاسُ نِيَامٌ، تَدْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ بِسَلاَمٍ
textEnglish: Spread peace (Salam), feed the hungry, maintain kinship ties, and pray during the night while people sleep: you will enter Paradise in complete peace.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2485, Sunan Ibn Majah 3251 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: The four golden keys to peaceful entry into Jannah unite communal kindness and private devotion.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: What warning or glad tiding is conveyed concerning smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الصَّدَقَةُ تَقَعُ فِي يَدِ الرَّحْمَنِ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَقَعَ فِي يَدِ السَّائِلِ
textEnglish: Charity falls into the Hand of the Most Merciful before it falls into the hand of the needy person.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1410, Sahih Muslim 1014 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Give charity with profound reverence; you are offering a direct transaction with your Lord.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: In what way does excellence in smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الْمُؤْمِنُ الْقَوِيُّ خَيْرٌ وَأَحَبُّ إِلَى اللَّهِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِ الضَّعِيفِ، وَفِي كُلٍّ خَيْرٌ
textEnglish: The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, though there is goodness in both. Strive for what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not lose heart.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2664 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Cultivate mental, moral, physical, and spiritual strength while maintaining humble reliance on Allah.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: How can one safeguard smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ سَرَّهُ أَنْ يُبْسَطَ لَهُ فِي رِزْقِهِ، وَأَنْ يُنْسَأَ لَهُ فِي أَثَرِهِ، فَلْيَصِلْ رَحِمَهُ
textEnglish: Whoever delights in having his provision expanded and his lifespan blessed and extended, let him maintain ties of kinship.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5986, Sahih Muslim 2557 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Kindness to relatives and family reconciliation draws barakah into time and livelihood.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: What essential principle transforms our approach to smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِذَا مَاتَ الإِنْسَانُ انْقَطَعَ عَنْهُ عَمَلُهُ إِلاَّ مِنْ ثَلاَثَةٍ: صَدَقَةٍ جَارِيَةٍ، أَوْ عِلْمٍ يُنْتَفَعُ بِهِ، أَوْ وَلَدٍ صَالِحٍ يَدْعُو لَهُ
textEnglish: When a human being dies, all his deeds cease except for three: recurring charity (Sadaqah Jariyah), beneficial knowledge left behind, or a righteous child who prays for him.
reference: Sahih Muslim 1631 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Invest your life in legacies that continue to shine and generate divine rewards after your earthly departure.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: Why is genuine devotion in smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّمَا الأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ، وَإِنَّمَا لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى
textEnglish: Actions are judged by motives and intentions, and every person will have only that which they intended.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1, Sahih Muslim 1907 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Purify your heart before every deed; a sincere intention transforms simple daily acts into perpetual worship.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: How does the heart find tranquility through smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الإِيمَانُ أَنْ تُؤْمِنَ بِاللَّهِ، وَمَلاَئِكَتِهِ، وَكُتُبِهِ، وَرُسُلِهِ، وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ، وَتُؤْمِنَ بِالْقَدَرِ خَيْرِهِ وَشَرِّهِ
textEnglish: Faith is that you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and divine destiny—both its prosperity and adversity.
reference: Sahih Muslim 8 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Conviction in Allah’s wisdom gives the believer unwavering calm during life’s unpredictable changes.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: What common pitfall did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ warn about in smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الرَّاحِمُونَ يَرْحَمُهُمُ الرَّحْمَنُ، ارْحَمُوا مَنْ فِي الأَرْضِ يَرْحَمْكُمْ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاءِ
textEnglish: The merciful will be shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Be merciful to those on earth, and the One in the heavens will be merciful to you.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1924, Sunan Abi Dawud 4941 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Compassion to all living beings is the golden key that unlocks divine mercy and forgiveness.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: How does moral beauty manifest through smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لاَ يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لأَخِيهِ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ
textEnglish: None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 13, Sahih Muslim 45 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Genuine faith cleanses the soul of jealousy and cultivates sincere goodwill toward all people.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: What eternal reward is promised for cultivating smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّ مِنْ خِيَارِكُمْ أَحْسَنَكُمْ أَخْلاَقًا
textEnglish: Indeed, the best and most beloved among you are those who possess the best character and manners.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 3559, Sahih Muslim 2321 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Gentleness, integrity, and warmth of character are the true reflection of a living faith.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: How can parents and mentors inspire smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الطُّهُورُ شَطْرُ الإِيمَانِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ تَمْلأُ الْمِيزَانَ
textEnglish: Purity is half of faith, and “Alhamdulillah” (Praise be to Allah) fills the divine scale of deeds.
reference: Sahih Muslim 223 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Inner and outer purification are intertwined; heartfelt gratitude tilts the eternal scale in your favor.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: What guidance did the Prophet ﷺ emphasize regarding consistency in smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: أَوَّلُ مَا يُحَاسَبُ بِهِ الْعَبْدُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ مِنْ عَمَلِهِ صَلاَتُهُ
textEnglish: The first matter for which the slave of Allah will be brought to account on the Day of Judgment is his prayer.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 413, Sunan an-Nasa’i 465 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Salah is your personal appointment with the Lord of the worlds; safeguard its punctuality and focus.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: How does divine mercy embrace those who strive in smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّ الدِّينَ يُسْرٌ، وَلَنْ يُشَادَّ الدِّينَ أَحَدٌ إِلاَّ غَلَبَهُ
textEnglish: Indeed, the religion is easy, and no one makes the religion overly difficult except that it will overcome him.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 39 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Adopt a steady, balanced pace of devotion; moderation sustains lifelong spiritual growth.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: In times of difficulty, how does smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لَيْسَ الْغِنَى عَنْ كَثْرَةِ الْعَرَضِ، وَلَكِنَّ الْغِنَى غِنَى النَّفْسِ
textEnglish: Richness is not about abundance of worldly possessions; true wealth is the richness of contentment in the soul.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6446, Sahih Muslim 1051 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Peace is never found in endless material craving, but in tranquility and satisfaction with what Allah gave.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: What reflection on the Hereafter is awakened by smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ فَلْيَقُلْ خَيْرًا أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ
textEnglish: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak what is beneficial or remain silent.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6018, Sahih Muslim 47 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Guarding speech protects relationships and preserves the dignity and purity of the heart.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: How does understanding smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَثَلُ الَّذِي يَذْكُرُ رَبَّهُ وَالَّذِي لاَ يَذْكُرُ رَبَّهُ مَثَلُ الْحَيِّ وَالْمَيِّتِ
textEnglish: The example of the one who remembers his Lord compared to the one who does not is like that of the living and the dead.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6407, Sahih Muslim 779 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Dhikr is the oxygen of the spiritual heart; without it, the inner being withers.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: What divine wisdom did the Prophet ﷺ reveal regarding smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَا يُصِيبُ الْمُسْلِمَ مِنْ نَصَبٍ وَلاَ وَصَبٍ وَلاَ هَمٍّ وَلاَ حَزَنٍ وَلاَ أَذًى حَتَّى الشَّوْكَةِ يُشَاكُهَا إِلاَّ كَفَّرَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مِنْ خَطَايَاهُ
textEnglish: No fatigue, illness, worry, grief, hurt, or distress befalls a believer—even the prick of a thorn—except that Allah expiates some of his sins through it.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5641, Sahih Muslim 2573 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Every silent patience during hardship is recognized, rewarded, and purified by the Most Merciful.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: How does consistent practice of smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: تَبَسُّمُكَ فِي وَجْهِ أَخِيكَ لَكَ صَدَقَةٌ
textEnglish: Your smiling in the face of your brother is charity for you.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1956 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Radiating warmth and gentle kindness costs nothing yet carries eternal divine reward.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: What spiritual remedy does smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الْمُسْلِمُ مَنْ سَلِمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِهِ وَيَدِهِ
textEnglish: The true Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hands other people are completely safe.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 10, Sahih Muslim 40 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Righteousness is verified when those around you live in safety from your harm and speech.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: Why is sincere commitment to smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
textEnglish: The best among you are those who learn the Quran and teach it to others.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5027 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Connecting yourself with the Book of Allah and sharing its light with others is the pinnacle of nobility.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: How did the noble Companions embody smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ سَلَكَ طَرِيقًا يَلْتَمِسُ فِيهِ عِلْمًا سَهَّلَ اللَّهُ لَهُ بِهِ طَرِيقًا إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ
textEnglish: Whoever travels a path seeking sacred knowledge, Allah makes smooth for him a path to Paradise.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2699 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Every moment dedicated to understanding faith and truth brings you closer to the gardens of Jannah.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: What warning or glad tiding is conveyed concerning smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لاَ تَغْضَبْ، فَرَدَّدَ مِرَارًا، قَالَ: لاَ تَغْضَبْ
textEnglish: A man said to the Prophet: “Advise me.” He said: “Do not become angry.” The man repeated his request several times, and each time he replied: “Do not become angry.”
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6116 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Mastery over impulsive anger preserves wisdom, protects relationships, and prevents regret.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: In what way does excellence in smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: اتَّقِ اللَّهَ حَيْثُمَا كُنْتَ، وَأَتْبِعِ السَّيِّئَةَ الْحَسَنَةَ تَمْحُهَا، وَخَالِقِ النَّاسَ بِخُلُقٍ حَسَنٍ
textEnglish: Be mindful of Allah wherever you are; follow an evil deed with a good one and it will erase it; and treat people with beautiful character.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1987 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Live with God-consciousness in private and public, rapidly correct missteps, and be gracious to all.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: How can one safeguard smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: كُلُّكُمْ رَاعٍ وَكُلُّكُمْ مَسْئُولٌ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهِ
textEnglish: Every one of you is a shepherd and guardian, and every one of you will be questioned concerning his flock.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 893, Sahih Muslim 1829 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Leadership is a sacred trust and responsibility of service, not privilege or authority.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: What essential principle transforms our approach to smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ إِذَا عَمِلَ أَحَدُكُمْ عَمَلاً أَنْ يُتْقِنَهُ
textEnglish: Verily, Allah loves that whenever any of you undertakes a work, he executes it with mastery and excellence (Itqan).
reference: Shu’ab al-Iman (Al-Bayhaqi 4929, Hasan) · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Excellence in profession, study, and daily duty is an act of devotion loved by the Creator.

subTopicTitle: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
question: Why is genuine devotion in smiling and pleasant words as charity and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الْحَيَاءُ لاَ يَأْتِي إِلاَّ بِخَيْرٍ
textEnglish: Modesty and conscience (Haya) bring nothing except goodness.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6117, Sahih Muslim 37 · Chapter 61: Smiling and Pleasant Words as Charity
keyLesson: Haya is a spiritual shield that restrains the soul from vulgarity and prompts noble conduct.

question: What spiritual wisdom did the Prophet ﷺ teach regarding removing harm from the pathway?
textArabic: إِنَّ الدِّينَ يُسْرٌ، وَلَنْ يُشَادَّ الدِّينَ أَحَدٌ إِلاَّ غَلَبَهُ
textEnglish: Indeed, the religion is easy, and no one makes the religion overly difficult except that it will overcome him.

textEnglish: Modesty and conscience (Haya) bring nothing except goodness.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6117, Sahih Muslim 37 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Haya is a spiritual shield that restrains the soul from vulgarity and prompts noble conduct.

question: What eternal reward is promised for cultivating removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ كَفَلَ يَتِيمًا لَهُ أَوْ لِغَيْرِهِ فَأَنَا وَهُوَ كَهَاتَيْنِ فِي الْجَنَّةِ
textEnglish: The one who cares for an orphan and myself will be together in Paradise like these two fingers (joining his index and middle finger).
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5304, Sahih Muslim 2983 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Caring for vulnerable orphans guarantees the closest companionship with the Prophet ﷺ in the highest Jannah.

question: How can parents and mentors inspire removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَا نَقَصَتْ صَدَقَةٌ مِنْ مَالٍ، وَمَا زَادَ اللَّهُ عَبْدًا بِعَفْوٍ إِلاَّ عِزًّا
textEnglish: Charity never decreases wealth; and Allah never increases a servant who forgives except in honor and elevation.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2588 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Generosity and forgiveness never degrade a person; they invoke divine barakah and nobility.

question: What guidance did the Prophet ﷺ emphasize regarding consistency in removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: احْفَظِ اللَّهَ يَحْفَظْكَ، احْفَظِ اللَّهَ تَجِدْهُ تُجَاهَكَ
textEnglish: Be mindful of Allah, and He will protect you. Be mindful of Allah, and you will find Him facing you in every need.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2516 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Honor Allah’s commands in times of ease, and He will deliver and comfort you in times of adversity.

question: How does divine mercy embrace those who strive in removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لَوْ أَنَّكُمْ تَوَكَّلُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ حَقَّ تَوَكُّلِهِ لَرَزَقَكُمْ كَمَا يَرْزُقُ الطَّيْرَ
textEnglish: If you were to rely upon Allah with true reliance (Tawakkul), He would provide for you just as He provides for birds: they depart hungry at dawn and return full at dusk.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2344, Sunan Ibn Majah 4164 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Combine practical effort with tranquil reliance upon the Ultimate Provider.

question: In times of difficulty, how does removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: أَفْشُوا السَّلاَمَ، وَأَطْعِمُوا الطَّعَامَ، وَصِلُوا الأَرْحَامَ، وَصَلُّوا بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّاسُ نِيَامٌ، تَدْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ بِسَلاَمٍ
textEnglish: Spread peace (Salam), feed the hungry, maintain kinship ties, and pray during the night while people sleep: you will enter Paradise in complete peace.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2485, Sunan Ibn Majah 3251 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: The four golden keys to peaceful entry into Jannah unite communal kindness and private devotion.

question: What reflection on the Hereafter is awakened by removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الصَّدَقَةُ تَقَعُ فِي يَدِ الرَّحْمَنِ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَقَعَ فِي يَدِ السَّائِلِ
textEnglish: Charity falls into the Hand of the Most Merciful before it falls into the hand of the needy person.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1410, Sahih Muslim 1014 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Give charity with profound reverence; you are offering a direct transaction with your Lord.

question: How does understanding removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الْمُؤْمِنُ الْقَوِيُّ خَيْرٌ وَأَحَبُّ إِلَى اللَّهِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِ الضَّعِيفِ، وَفِي كُلٍّ خَيْرٌ
textEnglish: The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, though there is goodness in both. Strive for what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not lose heart.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2664 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Cultivate mental, moral, physical, and spiritual strength while maintaining humble reliance on Allah.

question: What divine wisdom did the Prophet ﷺ reveal regarding removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ سَرَّهُ أَنْ يُبْسَطَ لَهُ فِي رِزْقِهِ، وَأَنْ يُنْسَأَ لَهُ فِي أَثَرِهِ، فَلْيَصِلْ رَحِمَهُ
textEnglish: Whoever delights in having his provision expanded and his lifespan blessed and extended, let him maintain ties of kinship.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5986, Sahih Muslim 2557 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Kindness to relatives and family reconciliation draws barakah into time and livelihood.

question: How does consistent practice of removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِذَا مَاتَ الإِنْسَانُ انْقَطَعَ عَنْهُ عَمَلُهُ إِلاَّ مِنْ ثَلاَثَةٍ: صَدَقَةٍ جَارِيَةٍ، أَوْ عِلْمٍ يُنْتَفَعُ بِهِ، أَوْ وَلَدٍ صَالِحٍ يَدْعُو لَهُ
textEnglish: When a human being dies, all his deeds cease except for three: recurring charity (Sadaqah Jariyah), beneficial knowledge left behind, or a righteous child who prays for him.
reference: Sahih Muslim 1631 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Invest your life in legacies that continue to shine and generate divine rewards after your earthly departure.

question: What spiritual remedy does removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّمَا الأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ، وَإِنَّمَا لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى
textEnglish: Actions are judged by motives and intentions, and every person will have only that which they intended.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1, Sahih Muslim 1907 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Purify your heart before every deed; a sincere intention transforms simple daily acts into perpetual worship.

question: Why is sincere commitment to removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الإِيمَانُ أَنْ تُؤْمِنَ بِاللَّهِ، وَمَلاَئِكَتِهِ، وَكُتُبِهِ، وَرُسُلِهِ، وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ، وَتُؤْمِنَ بِالْقَدَرِ خَيْرِهِ وَشَرِّهِ
textEnglish: Faith is that you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and divine destiny—both its prosperity and adversity.
reference: Sahih Muslim 8 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Conviction in Allah’s wisdom gives the believer unwavering calm during life’s unpredictable changes.

question: How did the noble Companions embody removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الرَّاحِمُونَ يَرْحَمُهُمُ الرَّحْمَنُ، ارْحَمُوا مَنْ فِي الأَرْضِ يَرْحَمْكُمْ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاءِ
textEnglish: The merciful will be shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Be merciful to those on earth, and the One in the heavens will be merciful to you.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1924, Sunan Abi Dawud 4941 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Compassion to all living beings is the golden key that unlocks divine mercy and forgiveness.

question: What warning or glad tiding is conveyed concerning removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لاَ يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لأَخِيهِ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ
textEnglish: None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 13, Sahih Muslim 45 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Genuine faith cleanses the soul of jealousy and cultivates sincere goodwill toward all people.

question: In what way does excellence in removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّ مِنْ خِيَارِكُمْ أَحْسَنَكُمْ أَخْلاَقًا
textEnglish: Indeed, the best and most beloved among you are those who possess the best character and manners.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 3559, Sahih Muslim 2321 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Gentleness, integrity, and warmth of character are the true reflection of a living faith.

question: How can one safeguard removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الطُّهُورُ شَطْرُ الإِيمَانِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ تَمْلأُ الْمِيزَانَ
textEnglish: Purity is half of faith, and “Alhamdulillah” (Praise be to Allah) fills the divine scale of deeds.
reference: Sahih Muslim 223 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Inner and outer purification are intertwined; heartfelt gratitude tilts the eternal scale in your favor.

question: What essential principle transforms our approach to removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: أَوَّلُ مَا يُحَاسَبُ بِهِ الْعَبْدُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ مِنْ عَمَلِهِ صَلاَتُهُ
textEnglish: The first matter for which the slave of Allah will be brought to account on the Day of Judgment is his prayer.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 413, Sunan an-Nasa’i 465 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Salah is your personal appointment with the Lord of the worlds; safeguard its punctuality and focus.

question: Why is genuine devotion in removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّ الدِّينَ يُسْرٌ، وَلَنْ يُشَادَّ الدِّينَ أَحَدٌ إِلاَّ غَلَبَهُ
textEnglish: Indeed, the religion is easy, and no one makes the religion overly difficult except that it will overcome him.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 39 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Adopt a steady, balanced pace of devotion; moderation sustains lifelong spiritual growth.

question: How does the heart find tranquility through removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لَيْسَ الْغِنَى عَنْ كَثْرَةِ الْعَرَضِ، وَلَكِنَّ الْغِنَى غِنَى النَّفْسِ
textEnglish: Richness is not about abundance of worldly possessions; true wealth is the richness of contentment in the soul.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6446, Sahih Muslim 1051 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Peace is never found in endless material craving, but in tranquility and satisfaction with what Allah gave.

question: What common pitfall did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ warn about in removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ فَلْيَقُلْ خَيْرًا أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ
textEnglish: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak what is beneficial or remain silent.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6018, Sahih Muslim 47 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Guarding speech protects relationships and preserves the dignity and purity of the heart.

question: How does moral beauty manifest through removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَثَلُ الَّذِي يَذْكُرُ رَبَّهُ وَالَّذِي لاَ يَذْكُرُ رَبَّهُ مَثَلُ الْحَيِّ وَالْمَيِّتِ
textEnglish: The example of the one who remembers his Lord compared to the one who does not is like that of the living and the dead.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6407, Sahih Muslim 779 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Dhikr is the oxygen of the spiritual heart; without it, the inner being withers.

question: What eternal reward is promised for cultivating removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَا يُصِيبُ الْمُسْلِمَ مِنْ نَصَبٍ وَلاَ وَصَبٍ وَلاَ هَمٍّ وَلاَ حَزَنٍ وَلاَ أَذًى حَتَّى الشَّوْكَةِ يُشَاكُهَا إِلاَّ كَفَّرَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مِنْ خَطَايَاهُ
textEnglish: No fatigue, illness, worry, grief, hurt, or distress befalls a believer—even the prick of a thorn—except that Allah expiates some of his sins through it.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5641, Sahih Muslim 2573 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Every silent patience during hardship is recognized, rewarded, and purified by the Most Merciful.

question: How can parents and mentors inspire removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: تَبَسُّمُكَ فِي وَجْهِ أَخِيكَ لَكَ صَدَقَةٌ
textEnglish: Your smiling in the face of your brother is charity for you.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1956 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Radiating warmth and gentle kindness costs nothing yet carries eternal divine reward.

question: What guidance did the Prophet ﷺ emphasize regarding consistency in removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الْمُسْلِمُ مَنْ سَلِمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِهِ وَيَدِهِ
textEnglish: The true Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hands other people are completely safe.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 10, Sahih Muslim 40 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Righteousness is verified when those around you live in safety from your harm and speech.

question: How does divine mercy embrace those who strive in removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
textEnglish: The best among you are those who learn the Quran and teach it to others.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5027 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Connecting yourself with the Book of Allah and sharing its light with others is the pinnacle of nobility.

question: In times of difficulty, how does removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ سَلَكَ طَرِيقًا يَلْتَمِسُ فِيهِ عِلْمًا سَهَّلَ اللَّهُ لَهُ بِهِ طَرِيقًا إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ
textEnglish: Whoever travels a path seeking sacred knowledge, Allah makes smooth for him a path to Paradise.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2699 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Every moment dedicated to understanding faith and truth brings you closer to the gardens of Jannah.

question: What reflection on the Hereafter is awakened by removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لاَ تَغْضَبْ، فَرَدَّدَ مِرَارًا، قَالَ: لاَ تَغْضَبْ
textEnglish: A man said to the Prophet: “Advise me.” He said: “Do not become angry.” The man repeated his request several times, and each time he replied: “Do not become angry.”
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6116 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Mastery over impulsive anger preserves wisdom, protects relationships, and prevents regret.

question: How does understanding removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: اتَّقِ اللَّهَ حَيْثُمَا كُنْتَ، وَأَتْبِعِ السَّيِّئَةَ الْحَسَنَةَ تَمْحُهَا، وَخَالِقِ النَّاسَ بِخُلُقٍ حَسَنٍ
textEnglish: Be mindful of Allah wherever you are; follow an evil deed with a good one and it will erase it; and treat people with beautiful character.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1987 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Live with God-consciousness in private and public, rapidly correct missteps, and be gracious to all.

question: What divine wisdom did the Prophet ﷺ reveal regarding removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: كُلُّكُمْ رَاعٍ وَكُلُّكُمْ مَسْئُولٌ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهِ
textEnglish: Every one of you is a shepherd and guardian, and every one of you will be questioned concerning his flock.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 893, Sahih Muslim 1829 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Leadership is a sacred trust and responsibility of service, not privilege or authority.

question: How does consistent practice of removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ إِذَا عَمِلَ أَحَدُكُمْ عَمَلاً أَنْ يُتْقِنَهُ
textEnglish: Verily, Allah loves that whenever any of you undertakes a work, he executes it with mastery and excellence (Itqan).
reference: Shu’ab al-Iman (Al-Bayhaqi 4929, Hasan) · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Excellence in profession, study, and daily duty is an act of devotion loved by the Creator.

question: What spiritual remedy does removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الْحَيَاءُ لاَ يَأْتِي إِلاَّ بِخَيْرٍ
textEnglish: Modesty and conscience (Haya) bring nothing except goodness.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6117, Sahih Muslim 37 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Haya is a spiritual shield that restrains the soul from vulgarity and prompts noble conduct.

question: Why is sincere commitment to removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ كَفَلَ يَتِيمًا لَهُ أَوْ لِغَيْرِهِ فَأَنَا وَهُوَ كَهَاتَيْنِ فِي الْجَنَّةِ
textEnglish: The one who cares for an orphan and myself will be together in Paradise like these two fingers (joining his index and middle finger).
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5304, Sahih Muslim 2983 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Caring for vulnerable orphans guarantees the closest companionship with the Prophet ﷺ in the highest Jannah.

question: How did the noble Companions embody removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَا نَقَصَتْ صَدَقَةٌ مِنْ مَالٍ، وَمَا زَادَ اللَّهُ عَبْدًا بِعَفْوٍ إِلاَّ عِزًّا
textEnglish: Charity never decreases wealth; and Allah never increases a servant who forgives except in honor and elevation.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2588 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Generosity and forgiveness never degrade a person; they invoke divine barakah and nobility.

question: What warning or glad tiding is conveyed concerning removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: احْفَظِ اللَّهَ يَحْفَظْكَ، احْفَظِ اللَّهَ تَجِدْهُ تُجَاهَكَ
textEnglish: Be mindful of Allah, and He will protect you. Be mindful of Allah, and you will find Him facing you in every need.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2516 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Honor Allah’s commands in times of ease, and He will deliver and comfort you in times of adversity.

question: In what way does excellence in removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لَوْ أَنَّكُمْ تَوَكَّلُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ حَقَّ تَوَكُّلِهِ لَرَزَقَكُمْ كَمَا يَرْزُقُ الطَّيْرَ
textEnglish: If you were to rely upon Allah with true reliance (Tawakkul), He would provide for you just as He provides for birds: they depart hungry at dawn and return full at dusk.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2344, Sunan Ibn Majah 4164 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Combine practical effort with tranquil reliance upon the Ultimate Provider.

question: How can one safeguard removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: أَفْشُوا السَّلاَمَ، وَأَطْعِمُوا الطَّعَامَ، وَصِلُوا الأَرْحَامَ، وَصَلُّوا بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّاسُ نِيَامٌ، تَدْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ بِسَلاَمٍ
textEnglish: Spread peace (Salam), feed the hungry, maintain kinship ties, and pray during the night while people sleep: you will enter Paradise in complete peace.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2485, Sunan Ibn Majah 3251 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: The four golden keys to peaceful entry into Jannah unite communal kindness and private devotion.

question: What essential principle transforms our approach to removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الصَّدَقَةُ تَقَعُ فِي يَدِ الرَّحْمَنِ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَقَعَ فِي يَدِ السَّائِلِ
textEnglish: Charity falls into the Hand of the Most Merciful before it falls into the hand of the needy person.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1410, Sahih Muslim 1014 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Give charity with profound reverence; you are offering a direct transaction with your Lord.

question: Why is genuine devotion in removing harm from the pathway and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الْمُؤْمِنُ الْقَوِيُّ خَيْرٌ وَأَحَبُّ إِلَى اللَّهِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِ الضَّعِيفِ، وَفِي كُلٍّ خَيْرٌ
textEnglish: The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, though there is goodness in both. Strive for what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not lose heart.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2664 · Chapter 62: Removing Harm from the Pathway
keyLesson: Cultivate mental, moral, physical, and spiritual strength while maintaining humble reliance on Allah.

question: What spiritual wisdom did the Prophet ﷺ teach regarding fasting the day of arafah?
textArabic: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
textEnglish: The best among you are those who learn the Quran and teach it to others.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5027 · Chapter 63: Fasting the Day of Arafah
keyLesson: Connecting yourself with the Book of Allah and sharing its light with others is the pinnacle of nobility.

question: What divine wisdom did the Prophet ﷺ reveal regarding fasting the day of arafah and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ سَلَكَ طَرِيقًا يَلْتَمِسُ فِيهِ عِلْمًا سَهَّلَ اللَّهُ لَهُ بِهِ طَرِيقًا إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ
textEnglish: Whoever travels a path seeking sacred knowledge, Allah makes smooth for him a path to Paradise.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2699 · Chapter 63: Fasting the Day of Arafah
keyLesson: Every moment dedicated to understanding faith and truth brings you closer to the gardens of Jannah.

question: How does consistent practice of fasting the day of arafah and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?

textArabic: احْفَظِ اللَّهَ يَحْفَظْكَ، احْفَظِ اللَّهَ تَجِدْهُ تُجَاهَكَ
textEnglish: Be mindful of Allah, and He will protect you. Be mindful of Allah, and you will find Him facing you in every need.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2516 · Chapter 63: Fasting the Day of Arafah
keyLesson: Honor Allah’s commands in times of ease, and He will deliver and comfort you in times of adversity.

question: Why is genuine devotion in fasting the day of arafah and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لَوْ أَنَّكُمْ تَوَكَّلُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ حَقَّ تَوَكُّلِهِ لَرَزَقَكُمْ كَمَا يَرْزُقُ الطَّيْرَ
textEnglish: If you were to rely upon Allah with true reliance (Tawakkul), He would provide for you just as He provides for birds: they depart hungry at dawn and return full at dusk.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2344, Sunan Ibn Majah 4164 · Chapter 63: Fasting the Day of Arafah
keyLesson: Combine practical effort with tranquil reliance upon the Ultimate Provider.

textArabic: أَفْشُوا السَّلاَمَ، وَأَطْعِمُوا الطَّعَامَ، وَصِلُوا الأَرْحَامَ، وَصَلُّوا بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّاسُ نِيَامٌ، تَدْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ بِسَلاَمٍ
textEnglish: Spread peace (Salam), feed the hungry, maintain kinship ties, and pray during the night while people sleep: you will enter Paradise in complete peace.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2485, Sunan Ibn Majah 3251 · Chapter 63: Fasting the Day of Arafah
keyLesson: The four golden keys to peaceful entry into Jannah unite communal kindness and private devotion.

question: What common pitfall did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ warn about in fasting the day of arafah and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الصَّدَقَةُ تَقَعُ فِي يَدِ الرَّحْمَنِ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَقَعَ فِي يَدِ السَّائِلِ
textEnglish: Charity falls into the Hand of the Most Merciful before it falls into the hand of the needy person.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1410, Sahih Muslim 1014 · Chapter 63: Fasting the Day of Arafah
keyLesson: Give charity with profound reverence; you are offering a direct transaction with your Lord.

textArabic: الْمُؤْمِنُ الْقَوِيُّ خَيْرٌ وَأَحَبُّ إِلَى اللَّهِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِ الضَّعِيفِ، وَفِي كُلٍّ خَيْرٌ
textEnglish: The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, though there is goodness in both. Strive for what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not lose heart.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2664 · Chapter 63: Fasting the Day of Arafah
keyLesson: Cultivate mental, moral, physical, and spiritual strength while maintaining humble reliance on Allah.

question: What eternal reward is promised for cultivating fasting the day of arafah and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ سَرَّهُ أَنْ يُبْسَطَ لَهُ فِي رِزْقِهِ، وَأَنْ يُنْسَأَ لَهُ فِي أَثَرِهِ، فَلْيَصِلْ رَحِمَهُ
textEnglish: Whoever delights in having his provision expanded and his lifespan blessed and extended, let him maintain ties of kinship.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5986, Sahih Muslim 2557 · Chapter 63: Fasting the Day of Arafah
keyLesson: Kindness to relatives and family reconciliation draws barakah into time and livelihood.

question: How can parents and mentors inspire fasting the day of arafah and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِذَا مَاتَ الإِنْسَانُ انْقَطَعَ عَنْهُ عَمَلُهُ إِلاَّ مِنْ ثَلاَثَةٍ: صَدَقَةٍ جَارِيَةٍ، أَوْ عِلْمٍ يُنْتَفَعُ بِهِ، أَوْ وَلَدٍ صَالِحٍ يَدْعُو لَهُ
textEnglish: When a human being dies, all his deeds cease except for three: recurring charity (Sadaqah Jariyah), beneficial knowledge left behind, or a righteous child who prays for him.
reference: Sahih Muslim 1631 · Chapter 63: Fasting the Day of Arafah
keyLesson: Invest your life in legacies that continue to shine and generate divine rewards after your earthly departure.

question: What guidance did the Prophet ﷺ emphasize regarding consistency in fasting the day of arafah and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّمَا الأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ، وَإِنَّمَا لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى
textEnglish: Actions are judged by motives and intentions, and every person will have only that which they intended.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1, Sahih Muslim 1907 · Chapter 63: Fasting the Day of Arafah
keyLesson: Purify your heart before every deed; a sincere intention transforms simple daily acts into perpetual worship.

question: How does divine mercy embrace those who strive in fasting the day of arafah and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الإِيمَانُ أَنْ تُؤْمِنَ بِاللَّهِ، وَمَلاَئِكَتِهِ، وَكُتُبِهِ، وَرُسُلِهِ، وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ، وَتُؤْمِنَ بِالْقَدَرِ خَيْرِهِ وَشَرِّهِ
textEnglish: Faith is that you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and divine destiny—both its prosperity and adversity.
reference: Sahih Muslim 8 · Chapter 63: Fasting the Day of Arafah
keyLesson: Conviction in Allah’s wisdom gives the believer unwavering calm during life’s unpredictable changes.

question: In times of difficulty, how does fasting the day of arafah and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الرَّاحِمُونَ يَرْحَمُهُمُ الرَّحْمَنُ، ارْحَمُوا مَنْ فِي الأَرْضِ يَرْحَمْكُمْ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاءِ
textEnglish: The merciful will be shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Be merciful to those on earth, and the One in the heavens will be merciful to you.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1924, Sunan Abi Dawud 4941 · Chapter 63: Fasting the Day of Arafah
keyLesson: Compassion to all living beings is the golden key that unlocks divine mercy and forgiveness.

question: What reflection on the Hereafter is awakened by fasting the day of arafah and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لاَ يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لأَخِيهِ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ
textEnglish: None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 13, Sahih Muslim 45 · Chapter 63: Fasting the Day of Arafah
keyLesson: Genuine faith cleanses the soul of jealousy and cultivates sincere goodwill toward all people.

question: How does understanding fasting the day of arafah and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّ مِنْ خِيَارِكُمْ أَحْسَنَكُمْ أَخْلاَقًا
textEnglish: Indeed, the best and most beloved among you are those who possess the best character and manners.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 3559, Sahih Muslim 2321 · Chapter 63: Fasting the Day of Arafah
keyLesson: Gentleness, integrity, and warmth of character are the true reflection of a living faith.

question: What divine wisdom did the Prophet ﷺ reveal regarding fasting the day of arafah and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الطُّهُورُ شَطْرُ الإِيمَانِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ تَمْلأُ الْمِيزَانَ
textEnglish: Purity is half of faith, and “Alhamdulillah” (Praise be to Allah) fills the divine scale of deeds.
reference: Sahih Muslim 223 · Chapter 63: Fasting the Day of Arafah
keyLesson: Inner and outer purification are intertwined; heartfelt gratitude tilts the eternal scale in your favor.

question: How does consistent practice of fasting the day of arafah and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: أَوَّلُ مَا يُحَاسَبُ بِهِ الْعَبْدُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ مِنْ عَمَلِهِ صَلاَتُهُ
textEnglish: The first matter for which the slave of Allah will be brought to account on the Day of Judgment is his prayer.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 413, Sunan an-Nasa’i 465 · Chapter 63: Fasting the Day of Arafah
keyLesson: Salah is your personal appointment with the Lord of the worlds; safeguard its punctuality and focus.

question: What spiritual remedy does fasting the day of arafah and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّ الدِّينَ يُسْرٌ، وَلَنْ يُشَادَّ الدِّينَ أَحَدٌ إِلاَّ غَلَبَهُ
textEnglish: Indeed, the religion is easy, and no one makes the religion overly difficult except that it will overcome him.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 39 · Chapter 63: Fasting the Day of Arafah
keyLesson: Adopt a steady, balanced pace of devotion; moderation sustains lifelong spiritual growth.

question: Why is sincere commitment to fasting the day of arafah and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لَيْسَ الْغِنَى عَنْ كَثْرَةِ الْعَرَضِ، وَلَكِنَّ الْغِنَى غِنَى النَّفْسِ
textEnglish: Richness is not about abundance of worldly possessions; true wealth is the richness of contentment in the soul.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6446, Sahih Muslim 1051 · Chapter 63: Fasting the Day of Arafah
keyLesson: Peace is never found in endless material craving, but in tranquility and satisfaction with what Allah gave.

question: How did the noble Companions embody fasting the day of arafah and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ فَلْيَقُلْ خَيْرًا أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ
textEnglish: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak what is beneficial or remain silent.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6018, Sahih Muslim 47 · Chapter 63: Fasting the Day of Arafah
keyLesson: Guarding speech protects relationships and preserves the dignity and purity of the heart.

question: What warning or glad tiding is conveyed concerning fasting the day of arafah and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَثَلُ الَّذِي يَذْكُرُ رَبَّهُ وَالَّذِي لاَ يَذْكُرُ رَبَّهُ مَثَلُ الْحَيِّ وَالْمَيِّتِ
textEnglish: The example of the one who remembers his Lord compared to the one who does not is like that of the living and the dead.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6407, Sahih Muslim 779 · Chapter 63: Fasting the Day of Arafah
keyLesson: Dhikr is the oxygen of the spiritual heart; without it, the inner being withers.

question: In what way does excellence in fasting the day of arafah and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَا يُصِيبُ الْمُسْلِمَ مِنْ نَصَبٍ وَلاَ وَصَبٍ وَلاَ هَمٍّ وَلاَ حَزَنٍ وَلاَ أَذًى حَتَّى الشَّوْكَةِ يُشَاكُهَا إِلاَّ كَفَّرَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مِنْ خَطَايَاهُ
textEnglish: No fatigue, illness, worry, grief, hurt, or distress befalls a believer—even the prick of a thorn—except that Allah expiates some of his sins through it.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5641, Sahih Muslim 2573 · Chapter 63: Fasting the Day of Arafah
keyLesson: Every silent patience during hardship is recognized, rewarded, and purified by the Most Merciful.

question: How can one safeguard fasting the day of arafah and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: تَبَسُّمُكَ فِي وَجْهِ أَخِيكَ لَكَ صَدَقَةٌ
textEnglish: Your smiling in the face of your brother is charity for you.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1956 · Chapter 63: Fasting the Day of Arafah
keyLesson: Radiating warmth and gentle kindness costs nothing yet carries eternal divine reward.

question: What essential principle transforms our approach to fasting the day of arafah and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الْمُسْلِمُ مَنْ سَلِمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِهِ وَيَدِهِ
textEnglish: The true Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hands other people are completely safe.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 10, Sahih Muslim 40 · Chapter 63: Fasting the Day of Arafah
keyLesson: Righteousness is verified when those around you live in safety from your harm and speech.

question: Why is genuine devotion in fasting the day of arafah and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
textEnglish: The best among you are those who learn the Quran and teach it to others.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5027 · Chapter 63: Fasting the Day of Arafah
keyLesson: Connecting yourself with the Book of Allah and sharing its light with others is the pinnacle of nobility.

question: How does the heart find tranquility through fasting the day of arafah and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ سَلَكَ طَرِيقًا يَلْتَمِسُ فِيهِ عِلْمًا سَهَّلَ اللَّهُ لَهُ بِهِ طَرِيقًا إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ
textEnglish: Whoever travels a path seeking sacred knowledge, Allah makes smooth for him a path to Paradise.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2699 · Chapter 63: Fasting the Day of Arafah
keyLesson: Every moment dedicated to understanding faith and truth brings you closer to the gardens of Jannah.

question: What common pitfall did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ warn about in fasting the day of arafah and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لاَ تَغْضَبْ، فَرَدَّدَ مِرَارًا، قَالَ: لاَ تَغْضَبْ
textEnglish: A man said to the Prophet: “Advise me.” He said: “Do not become angry.” The man repeated his request several times, and each time he replied: “Do not become angry.”
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6116 · Chapter 63: Fasting the Day of Arafah
keyLesson: Mastery over impulsive anger preserves wisdom, protects relationships, and prevents regret.

question: How does moral beauty manifest through fasting the day of arafah and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: اتَّقِ اللَّهَ حَيْثُمَا كُنْتَ، وَأَتْبِعِ السَّيِّئَةَ الْحَسَنَةَ تَمْحُهَا، وَخَالِقِ النَّاسَ بِخُلُقٍ حَسَنٍ
textEnglish: Be mindful of Allah wherever you are; follow an evil deed with a good one and it will erase it; and treat people with beautiful character.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1987 · Chapter 63: Fasting the Day of Arafah
keyLesson: Live with God-consciousness in private and public, rapidly correct missteps, and be gracious to all.

question: What eternal reward is promised for cultivating fasting the day of arafah and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: كُلُّكُمْ رَاعٍ وَكُلُّكُمْ مَسْئُولٌ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهِ
textEnglish: Every one of you is a shepherd and guardian, and every one of you will be questioned concerning his flock.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 893, Sahih Muslim 1829 · Chapter 63: Fasting the Day of Arafah
keyLesson: Leadership is a sacred trust and responsibility of service, not privilege or authority.

question: How can parents and mentors inspire fasting the day of arafah and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ إِذَا عَمِلَ أَحَدُكُمْ عَمَلاً أَنْ يُتْقِنَهُ
textEnglish: Verily, Allah loves that whenever any of you undertakes a work, he executes it with mastery and excellence (Itqan).
reference: Shu’ab al-Iman (Al-Bayhaqi 4929, Hasan) · Chapter 63: Fasting the Day of Arafah
keyLesson: Excellence in profession, study, and daily duty is an act of devotion loved by the Creator.

question: What guidance did the Prophet ﷺ emphasize regarding consistency in fasting the day of arafah and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الْحَيَاءُ لاَ يَأْتِي إِلاَّ بِخَيْرٍ
textEnglish: Modesty and conscience (Haya) bring nothing except goodness.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6117, Sahih Muslim 37 · Chapter 63: Fasting the Day of Arafah
keyLesson: Haya is a spiritual shield that restrains the soul from vulgarity and prompts noble conduct.

question: How does divine mercy embrace those who strive in fasting the day of arafah and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ كَفَلَ يَتِيمًا لَهُ أَوْ لِغَيْرِهِ فَأَنَا وَهُوَ كَهَاتَيْنِ فِي الْجَنَّةِ
textEnglish: The one who cares for an orphan and myself will be together in Paradise like these two fingers (joining his index and middle finger).
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5304, Sahih Muslim 2983 · Chapter 63: Fasting the Day of Arafah
keyLesson: Caring for vulnerable orphans guarantees the closest companionship with the Prophet ﷺ in the highest Jannah.

question: In times of difficulty, how does fasting the day of arafah and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَا نَقَصَتْ صَدَقَةٌ مِنْ مَالٍ، وَمَا زَادَ اللَّهُ عَبْدًا بِعَفْوٍ إِلاَّ عِزًّا
textEnglish: Charity never decreases wealth; and Allah never increases a servant who forgives except in honor and elevation.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2588 · Chapter 63: Fasting the Day of Arafah
keyLesson: Generosity and forgiveness never degrade a person; they invoke divine barakah and nobility.

question: What reflection on the Hereafter is awakened by fasting the day of arafah and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?

textEnglish: Be mindful of Allah, and He will protect you. Be mindful of Allah, and you will find Him facing you in every need.
