keyLesson: Caring for vulnerable orphans guarantees the closest companionship with the Prophet ﷺ in the highest Jannah.

question: What eternal reward is promised for cultivating humility and eradicating pride (kibr) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَا نَقَصَتْ صَدَقَةٌ مِنْ مَالٍ، وَمَا زَادَ اللَّهُ عَبْدًا بِعَفْوٍ إِلاَّ عِزًّا
textEnglish: Charity never decreases wealth; and Allah never increases a servant who forgives except in honor and elevation.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2588 · Chapter 105: Humility and Eradicating Pride (Kibr)
keyLesson: Generosity and forgiveness never degrade a person; they invoke divine barakah and nobility.

question: How can parents and mentors inspire humility and eradicating pride (kibr) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: احْفَظِ اللَّهَ يَحْفَظْكَ، احْفَظِ اللَّهَ تَجِدْهُ تُجَاهَكَ
textEnglish: Be mindful of Allah, and He will protect you. Be mindful of Allah, and you will find Him facing you in every need.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2516 · Chapter 105: Humility and Eradicating Pride (Kibr)
keyLesson: Honor Allah’s commands in times of ease, and He will deliver and comfort you in times of adversity.

question: What guidance did the Prophet ﷺ emphasize regarding consistency in humility and eradicating pride (kibr) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لَوْ أَنَّكُمْ تَوَكَّلُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ حَقَّ تَوَكُّلِهِ لَرَزَقَكُمْ كَمَا يَرْزُقُ الطَّيْرَ
textEnglish: If you were to rely upon Allah with true reliance (Tawakkul), He would provide for you just as He provides for birds: they depart hungry at dawn and return full at dusk.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2344, Sunan Ibn Majah 4164 · Chapter 105: Humility and Eradicating Pride (Kibr)
keyLesson: Combine practical effort with tranquil reliance upon the Ultimate Provider.

question: How does divine mercy embrace those who strive in humility and eradicating pride (kibr) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: أَفْشُوا السَّلاَمَ، وَأَطْعِمُوا الطَّعَامَ، وَصِلُوا الأَرْحَامَ، وَصَلُّوا بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّاسُ نِيَامٌ، تَدْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ بِسَلاَمٍ
textEnglish: Spread peace (Salam), feed the hungry, maintain kinship ties, and pray during the night while people sleep: you will enter Paradise in complete peace.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2485, Sunan Ibn Majah 3251 · Chapter 105: Humility and Eradicating Pride (Kibr)
keyLesson: The four golden keys to peaceful entry into Jannah unite communal kindness and private devotion.

question: In times of difficulty, how does humility and eradicating pride (kibr) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الصَّدَقَةُ تَقَعُ فِي يَدِ الرَّحْمَنِ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَقَعَ فِي يَدِ السَّائِلِ
textEnglish: Charity falls into the Hand of the Most Merciful before it falls into the hand of the needy person.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1410, Sahih Muslim 1014 · Chapter 105: Humility and Eradicating Pride (Kibr)
keyLesson: Give charity with profound reverence; you are offering a direct transaction with your Lord.

question: What reflection on the Hereafter is awakened by humility and eradicating pride (kibr) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الْمُؤْمِنُ الْقَوِيُّ خَيْرٌ وَأَحَبُّ إِلَى اللَّهِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِ الضَّعِيفِ، وَفِي كُلٍّ خَيْرٌ
textEnglish: The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, though there is goodness in both. Strive for what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not lose heart.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2664 · Chapter 105: Humility and Eradicating Pride (Kibr)
keyLesson: Cultivate mental, moral, physical, and spiritual strength while maintaining humble reliance on Allah.

question: How does understanding humility and eradicating pride (kibr) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ سَرَّهُ أَنْ يُبْسَطَ لَهُ فِي رِزْقِهِ، وَأَنْ يُنْسَأَ لَهُ فِي أَثَرِهِ، فَلْيَصِلْ رَحِمَهُ
textEnglish: Whoever delights in having his provision expanded and his lifespan blessed and extended, let him maintain ties of kinship.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5986, Sahih Muslim 2557 · Chapter 105: Humility and Eradicating Pride (Kibr)
keyLesson: Kindness to relatives and family reconciliation draws barakah into time and livelihood.

question: What divine wisdom did the Prophet ﷺ reveal regarding humility and eradicating pride (kibr) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِذَا مَاتَ الإِنْسَانُ انْقَطَعَ عَنْهُ عَمَلُهُ إِلاَّ مِنْ ثَلاَثَةٍ: صَدَقَةٍ جَارِيَةٍ، أَوْ عِلْمٍ يُنْتَفَعُ بِهِ، أَوْ وَلَدٍ صَالِحٍ يَدْعُو لَهُ
textEnglish: When a human being dies, all his deeds cease except for three: recurring charity (Sadaqah Jariyah), beneficial knowledge left behind, or a righteous child who prays for him.
reference: Sahih Muslim 1631 · Chapter 105: Humility and Eradicating Pride (Kibr)
keyLesson: Invest your life in legacies that continue to shine and generate divine rewards after your earthly departure.

question: How does consistent practice of humility and eradicating pride (kibr) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّمَا الأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ، وَإِنَّمَا لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى
textEnglish: Actions are judged by motives and intentions, and every person will have only that which they intended.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1, Sahih Muslim 1907 · Chapter 105: Humility and Eradicating Pride (Kibr)
keyLesson: Purify your heart before every deed; a sincere intention transforms simple daily acts into perpetual worship.

question: What spiritual remedy does humility and eradicating pride (kibr) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الإِيمَانُ أَنْ تُؤْمِنَ بِاللَّهِ، وَمَلاَئِكَتِهِ، وَكُتُبِهِ، وَرُسُلِهِ، وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ، وَتُؤْمِنَ بِالْقَدَرِ خَيْرِهِ وَشَرِّهِ
textEnglish: Faith is that you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and divine destiny—both its prosperity and adversity.
reference: Sahih Muslim 8 · Chapter 105: Humility and Eradicating Pride (Kibr)
keyLesson: Conviction in Allah’s wisdom gives the believer unwavering calm during life’s unpredictable changes.

question: Why is sincere commitment to humility and eradicating pride (kibr) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الرَّاحِمُونَ يَرْحَمُهُمُ الرَّحْمَنُ، ارْحَمُوا مَنْ فِي الأَرْضِ يَرْحَمْكُمْ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاءِ
textEnglish: The merciful will be shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Be merciful to those on earth, and the One in the heavens will be merciful to you.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1924, Sunan Abi Dawud 4941 · Chapter 105: Humility and Eradicating Pride (Kibr)
keyLesson: Compassion to all living beings is the golden key that unlocks divine mercy and forgiveness.

question: How did the noble Companions embody humility and eradicating pride (kibr) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لاَ يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لأَخِيهِ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ
textEnglish: None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 13, Sahih Muslim 45 · Chapter 105: Humility and Eradicating Pride (Kibr)
keyLesson: Genuine faith cleanses the soul of jealousy and cultivates sincere goodwill toward all people.

question: What warning or glad tiding is conveyed concerning humility and eradicating pride (kibr) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّ مِنْ خِيَارِكُمْ أَحْسَنَكُمْ أَخْلاَقًا
textEnglish: Indeed, the best and most beloved among you are those who possess the best character and manners.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 3559, Sahih Muslim 2321 · Chapter 105: Humility and Eradicating Pride (Kibr)
keyLesson: Gentleness, integrity, and warmth of character are the true reflection of a living faith.

question: In what way does excellence in humility and eradicating pride (kibr) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الطُّهُورُ شَطْرُ الإِيمَانِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ تَمْلأُ الْمِيزَانَ
textEnglish: Purity is half of faith, and “Alhamdulillah” (Praise be to Allah) fills the divine scale of deeds.
reference: Sahih Muslim 223 · Chapter 105: Humility and Eradicating Pride (Kibr)
keyLesson: Inner and outer purification are intertwined; heartfelt gratitude tilts the eternal scale in your favor.

question: How can one safeguard humility and eradicating pride (kibr) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: أَوَّلُ مَا يُحَاسَبُ بِهِ الْعَبْدُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ مِنْ عَمَلِهِ صَلاَتُهُ
textEnglish: The first matter for which the slave of Allah will be brought to account on the Day of Judgment is his prayer.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 413, Sunan an-Nasa’i 465 · Chapter 105: Humility and Eradicating Pride (Kibr)
keyLesson: Salah is your personal appointment with the Lord of the worlds; safeguard its punctuality and focus.

question: What essential principle transforms our approach to humility and eradicating pride (kibr) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّ الدِّينَ يُسْرٌ، وَلَنْ يُشَادَّ الدِّينَ أَحَدٌ إِلاَّ غَلَبَهُ
textEnglish: Indeed, the religion is easy, and no one makes the religion overly difficult except that it will overcome him.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 39 · Chapter 105: Humility and Eradicating Pride (Kibr)
keyLesson: Adopt a steady, balanced pace of devotion; moderation sustains lifelong spiritual growth.

question: Why is genuine devotion in humility and eradicating pride (kibr) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لَيْسَ الْغِنَى عَنْ كَثْرَةِ الْعَرَضِ، وَلَكِنَّ الْغِنَى غِنَى النَّفْسِ
textEnglish: Richness is not about abundance of worldly possessions; true wealth is the richness of contentment in the soul.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6446, Sahih Muslim 1051 · Chapter 105: Humility and Eradicating Pride (Kibr)
keyLesson: Peace is never found in endless material craving, but in tranquility and satisfaction with what Allah gave.

question: How does the heart find tranquility through humility and eradicating pride (kibr) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ فَلْيَقُلْ خَيْرًا أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ
textEnglish: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak what is beneficial or remain silent.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6018, Sahih Muslim 47 · Chapter 105: Humility and Eradicating Pride (Kibr)
keyLesson: Guarding speech protects relationships and preserves the dignity and purity of the heart.

question: What common pitfall did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ warn about in humility and eradicating pride (kibr) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَثَلُ الَّذِي يَذْكُرُ رَبَّهُ وَالَّذِي لاَ يَذْكُرُ رَبَّهُ مَثَلُ الْحَيِّ وَالْمَيِّتِ
textEnglish: The example of the one who remembers his Lord compared to the one who does not is like that of the living and the dead.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6407, Sahih Muslim 779 · Chapter 105: Humility and Eradicating Pride (Kibr)
keyLesson: Dhikr is the oxygen of the spiritual heart; without it, the inner being withers.

question: How does moral beauty manifest through humility and eradicating pride (kibr) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَا يُصِيبُ الْمُسْلِمَ مِنْ نَصَبٍ وَلاَ وَصَبٍ وَلاَ هَمٍّ وَلاَ حَزَنٍ وَلاَ أَذًى حَتَّى الشَّوْكَةِ يُشَاكُهَا إِلاَّ كَفَّرَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مِنْ خَطَايَاهُ
textEnglish: No fatigue, illness, worry, grief, hurt, or distress befalls a believer—even the prick of a thorn—except that Allah expiates some of his sins through it.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5641, Sahih Muslim 2573 · Chapter 105: Humility and Eradicating Pride (Kibr)
keyLesson: Every silent patience during hardship is recognized, rewarded, and purified by the Most Merciful.

question: What eternal reward is promised for cultivating humility and eradicating pride (kibr) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: تَبَسُّمُكَ فِي وَجْهِ أَخِيكَ لَكَ صَدَقَةٌ
textEnglish: Your smiling in the face of your brother is charity for you.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1956 · Chapter 105: Humility and Eradicating Pride (Kibr)
keyLesson: Radiating warmth and gentle kindness costs nothing yet carries eternal divine reward.

question: How can parents and mentors inspire humility and eradicating pride (kibr) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الْمُسْلِمُ مَنْ سَلِمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِهِ وَيَدِهِ
textEnglish: The true Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hands other people are completely safe.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 10, Sahih Muslim 40 · Chapter 105: Humility and Eradicating Pride (Kibr)
keyLesson: Righteousness is verified when those around you live in safety from your harm and speech.

question: What guidance did the Prophet ﷺ emphasize regarding consistency in humility and eradicating pride (kibr) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
textEnglish: The best among you are those who learn the Quran and teach it to others.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5027 · Chapter 105: Humility and Eradicating Pride (Kibr)
keyLesson: Connecting yourself with the Book of Allah and sharing its light with others is the pinnacle of nobility.

question: How does divine mercy embrace those who strive in humility and eradicating pride (kibr) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ سَلَكَ طَرِيقًا يَلْتَمِسُ فِيهِ عِلْمًا سَهَّلَ اللَّهُ لَهُ بِهِ طَرِيقًا إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ
textEnglish: Whoever travels a path seeking sacred knowledge, Allah makes smooth for him a path to Paradise.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2699 · Chapter 105: Humility and Eradicating Pride (Kibr)
keyLesson: Every moment dedicated to understanding faith and truth brings you closer to the gardens of Jannah.

question: In times of difficulty, how does humility and eradicating pride (kibr) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لاَ تَغْضَبْ، فَرَدَّدَ مِرَارًا، قَالَ: لاَ تَغْضَبْ
textEnglish: A man said to the Prophet: “Advise me.” He said: “Do not become angry.” The man repeated his request several times, and each time he replied: “Do not become angry.”
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6116 · Chapter 105: Humility and Eradicating Pride (Kibr)
keyLesson: Mastery over impulsive anger preserves wisdom, protects relationships, and prevents regret.

question: What reflection on the Hereafter is awakened by humility and eradicating pride (kibr) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: اتَّقِ اللَّهَ حَيْثُمَا كُنْتَ، وَأَتْبِعِ السَّيِّئَةَ الْحَسَنَةَ تَمْحُهَا، وَخَالِقِ النَّاسَ بِخُلُقٍ حَسَنٍ
textEnglish: Be mindful of Allah wherever you are; follow an evil deed with a good one and it will erase it; and treat people with beautiful character.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1987 · Chapter 105: Humility and Eradicating Pride (Kibr)
keyLesson: Live with God-consciousness in private and public, rapidly correct missteps, and be gracious to all.

question: How does understanding humility and eradicating pride (kibr) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: كُلُّكُمْ رَاعٍ وَكُلُّكُمْ مَسْئُولٌ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهِ
textEnglish: Every one of you is a shepherd and guardian, and every one of you will be questioned concerning his flock.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 893, Sahih Muslim 1829 · Chapter 105: Humility and Eradicating Pride (Kibr)
keyLesson: Leadership is a sacred trust and responsibility of service, not privilege or authority.

question: What divine wisdom did the Prophet ﷺ reveal regarding humility and eradicating pride (kibr) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ إِذَا عَمِلَ أَحَدُكُمْ عَمَلاً أَنْ يُتْقِنَهُ
textEnglish: Verily, Allah loves that whenever any of you undertakes a work, he executes it with mastery and excellence (Itqan).
reference: Shu’ab al-Iman (Al-Bayhaqi 4929, Hasan) · Chapter 105: Humility and Eradicating Pride (Kibr)
keyLesson: Excellence in profession, study, and daily duty is an act of devotion loved by the Creator.

question: How does consistent practice of humility and eradicating pride (kibr) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الْحَيَاءُ لاَ يَأْتِي إِلاَّ بِخَيْرٍ
textEnglish: Modesty and conscience (Haya) bring nothing except goodness.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6117, Sahih Muslim 37 · Chapter 105: Humility and Eradicating Pride (Kibr)
keyLesson: Haya is a spiritual shield that restrains the soul from vulgarity and prompts noble conduct.

question: What spiritual remedy does humility and eradicating pride (kibr) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ كَفَلَ يَتِيمًا لَهُ أَوْ لِغَيْرِهِ فَأَنَا وَهُوَ كَهَاتَيْنِ فِي الْجَنَّةِ
textEnglish: The one who cares for an orphan and myself will be together in Paradise like these two fingers (joining his index and middle finger).
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5304, Sahih Muslim 2983 · Chapter 105: Humility and Eradicating Pride (Kibr)
keyLesson: Caring for vulnerable orphans guarantees the closest companionship with the Prophet ﷺ in the highest Jannah.

textEnglish: Be mindful of Allah, and He will protect you. Be mindful of Allah, and you will find Him facing you in every need.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2516 · Chapter 105: Humility and Eradicating Pride (Kibr)
keyLesson: Honor Allah’s commands in times of ease, and He will deliver and comfort you in times of adversity.

keyLesson: Cultivate mental, moral, physical, and spiritual strength while maintaining humble reliance on Allah.

question: Why is genuine devotion in humility and eradicating pride (kibr) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ سَرَّهُ أَنْ يُبْسَطَ لَهُ فِي رِزْقِهِ، وَأَنْ يُنْسَأَ لَهُ فِي أَثَرِهِ، فَلْيَصِلْ رَحِمَهُ
textEnglish: Whoever delights in having his provision expanded and his lifespan blessed and extended, let him maintain ties of kinship.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5986, Sahih Muslim 2557 · Chapter 105: Humility and Eradicating Pride (Kibr)
keyLesson: Kindness to relatives and family reconciliation draws barakah into time and livelihood.

question: What spiritual wisdom did the Prophet ﷺ teach regarding guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah)?
textArabic: مَنْ سَلَكَ طَرِيقًا يَلْتَمِسُ فِيهِ عِلْمًا سَهَّلَ اللَّهُ لَهُ بِهِ طَرِيقًا إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ
textEnglish: Whoever travels a path seeking sacred knowledge, Allah makes smooth for him a path to Paradise.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2699 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Every moment dedicated to understanding faith and truth brings you closer to the gardens of Jannah.

question: What divine wisdom did the Prophet ﷺ reveal regarding guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لاَ تَغْضَبْ، فَرَدَّدَ مِرَارًا، قَالَ: لاَ تَغْضَبْ
textEnglish: A man said to the Prophet: “Advise me.” He said: “Do not become angry.” The man repeated his request several times, and each time he replied: “Do not become angry.”
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6116 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Mastery over impulsive anger preserves wisdom, protects relationships, and prevents regret.

question: How does consistent practice of guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: اتَّقِ اللَّهَ حَيْثُمَا كُنْتَ، وَأَتْبِعِ السَّيِّئَةَ الْحَسَنَةَ تَمْحُهَا، وَخَالِقِ النَّاسَ بِخُلُقٍ حَسَنٍ
textEnglish: Be mindful of Allah wherever you are; follow an evil deed with a good one and it will erase it; and treat people with beautiful character.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1987 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Live with God-consciousness in private and public, rapidly correct missteps, and be gracious to all.

question: What spiritual remedy does guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: كُلُّكُمْ رَاعٍ وَكُلُّكُمْ مَسْئُولٌ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهِ
textEnglish: Every one of you is a shepherd and guardian, and every one of you will be questioned concerning his flock.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 893, Sahih Muslim 1829 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Leadership is a sacred trust and responsibility of service, not privilege or authority.

question: Why is sincere commitment to guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ إِذَا عَمِلَ أَحَدُكُمْ عَمَلاً أَنْ يُتْقِنَهُ
textEnglish: Verily, Allah loves that whenever any of you undertakes a work, he executes it with mastery and excellence (Itqan).
reference: Shu’ab al-Iman (Al-Bayhaqi 4929, Hasan) · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Excellence in profession, study, and daily duty is an act of devotion loved by the Creator.

question: How did the noble Companions embody guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الْحَيَاءُ لاَ يَأْتِي إِلاَّ بِخَيْرٍ
textEnglish: Modesty and conscience (Haya) bring nothing except goodness.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6117, Sahih Muslim 37 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Haya is a spiritual shield that restrains the soul from vulgarity and prompts noble conduct.

question: What warning or glad tiding is conveyed concerning guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ كَفَلَ يَتِيمًا لَهُ أَوْ لِغَيْرِهِ فَأَنَا وَهُوَ كَهَاتَيْنِ فِي الْجَنَّةِ
textEnglish: The one who cares for an orphan and myself will be together in Paradise like these two fingers (joining his index and middle finger).
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5304, Sahih Muslim 2983 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Caring for vulnerable orphans guarantees the closest companionship with the Prophet ﷺ in the highest Jannah.

question: In what way does excellence in guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَا نَقَصَتْ صَدَقَةٌ مِنْ مَالٍ، وَمَا زَادَ اللَّهُ عَبْدًا بِعَفْوٍ إِلاَّ عِزًّا
textEnglish: Charity never decreases wealth; and Allah never increases a servant who forgives except in honor and elevation.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2588 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Generosity and forgiveness never degrade a person; they invoke divine barakah and nobility.

question: How can one safeguard guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: احْفَظِ اللَّهَ يَحْفَظْكَ، احْفَظِ اللَّهَ تَجِدْهُ تُجَاهَكَ
textEnglish: Be mindful of Allah, and He will protect you. Be mindful of Allah, and you will find Him facing you in every need.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2516 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Honor Allah’s commands in times of ease, and He will deliver and comfort you in times of adversity.

question: What essential principle transforms our approach to guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لَوْ أَنَّكُمْ تَوَكَّلُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ حَقَّ تَوَكُّلِهِ لَرَزَقَكُمْ كَمَا يَرْزُقُ الطَّيْرَ
textEnglish: If you were to rely upon Allah with true reliance (Tawakkul), He would provide for you just as He provides for birds: they depart hungry at dawn and return full at dusk.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2344, Sunan Ibn Majah 4164 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Combine practical effort with tranquil reliance upon the Ultimate Provider.

question: Why is genuine devotion in guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: أَفْشُوا السَّلاَمَ، وَأَطْعِمُوا الطَّعَامَ، وَصِلُوا الأَرْحَامَ، وَصَلُّوا بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّاسُ نِيَامٌ، تَدْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ بِسَلاَمٍ
textEnglish: Spread peace (Salam), feed the hungry, maintain kinship ties, and pray during the night while people sleep: you will enter Paradise in complete peace.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2485, Sunan Ibn Majah 3251 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: The four golden keys to peaceful entry into Jannah unite communal kindness and private devotion.

question: How does the heart find tranquility through guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الصَّدَقَةُ تَقَعُ فِي يَدِ الرَّحْمَنِ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَقَعَ فِي يَدِ السَّائِلِ
textEnglish: Charity falls into the Hand of the Most Merciful before it falls into the hand of the needy person.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1410, Sahih Muslim 1014 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Give charity with profound reverence; you are offering a direct transaction with your Lord.

question: What common pitfall did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ warn about in guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الْمُؤْمِنُ الْقَوِيُّ خَيْرٌ وَأَحَبُّ إِلَى اللَّهِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِ الضَّعِيفِ، وَفِي كُلٍّ خَيْرٌ
textEnglish: The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, though there is goodness in both. Strive for what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not lose heart.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2664 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Cultivate mental, moral, physical, and spiritual strength while maintaining humble reliance on Allah.

question: How does moral beauty manifest through guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ سَرَّهُ أَنْ يُبْسَطَ لَهُ فِي رِزْقِهِ، وَأَنْ يُنْسَأَ لَهُ فِي أَثَرِهِ، فَلْيَصِلْ رَحِمَهُ
textEnglish: Whoever delights in having his provision expanded and his lifespan blessed and extended, let him maintain ties of kinship.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5986, Sahih Muslim 2557 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Kindness to relatives and family reconciliation draws barakah into time and livelihood.

question: What eternal reward is promised for cultivating guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِذَا مَاتَ الإِنْسَانُ انْقَطَعَ عَنْهُ عَمَلُهُ إِلاَّ مِنْ ثَلاَثَةٍ: صَدَقَةٍ جَارِيَةٍ، أَوْ عِلْمٍ يُنْتَفَعُ بِهِ، أَوْ وَلَدٍ صَالِحٍ يَدْعُو لَهُ
textEnglish: When a human being dies, all his deeds cease except for three: recurring charity (Sadaqah Jariyah), beneficial knowledge left behind, or a righteous child who prays for him.
reference: Sahih Muslim 1631 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Invest your life in legacies that continue to shine and generate divine rewards after your earthly departure.

question: How can parents and mentors inspire guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّمَا الأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ، وَإِنَّمَا لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى
textEnglish: Actions are judged by motives and intentions, and every person will have only that which they intended.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1, Sahih Muslim 1907 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Purify your heart before every deed; a sincere intention transforms simple daily acts into perpetual worship.

question: What guidance did the Prophet ﷺ emphasize regarding consistency in guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الإِيمَانُ أَنْ تُؤْمِنَ بِاللَّهِ، وَمَلاَئِكَتِهِ، وَكُتُبِهِ، وَرُسُلِهِ، وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ، وَتُؤْمِنَ بِالْقَدَرِ خَيْرِهِ وَشَرِّهِ
textEnglish: Faith is that you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and divine destiny—both its prosperity and adversity.
reference: Sahih Muslim 8 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Conviction in Allah’s wisdom gives the believer unwavering calm during life’s unpredictable changes.

question: How does divine mercy embrace those who strive in guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الرَّاحِمُونَ يَرْحَمُهُمُ الرَّحْمَنُ، ارْحَمُوا مَنْ فِي الأَرْضِ يَرْحَمْكُمْ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاءِ
textEnglish: The merciful will be shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Be merciful to those on earth, and the One in the heavens will be merciful to you.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1924, Sunan Abi Dawud 4941 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Compassion to all living beings is the golden key that unlocks divine mercy and forgiveness.

question: In times of difficulty, how does guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لاَ يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لأَخِيهِ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ
textEnglish: None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 13, Sahih Muslim 45 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Genuine faith cleanses the soul of jealousy and cultivates sincere goodwill toward all people.

question: What reflection on the Hereafter is awakened by guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّ مِنْ خِيَارِكُمْ أَحْسَنَكُمْ أَخْلاَقًا
textEnglish: Indeed, the best and most beloved among you are those who possess the best character and manners.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 3559, Sahih Muslim 2321 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Gentleness, integrity, and warmth of character are the true reflection of a living faith.

question: How does understanding guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الطُّهُورُ شَطْرُ الإِيمَانِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ تَمْلأُ الْمِيزَانَ
textEnglish: Purity is half of faith, and “Alhamdulillah” (Praise be to Allah) fills the divine scale of deeds.
reference: Sahih Muslim 223 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Inner and outer purification are intertwined; heartfelt gratitude tilts the eternal scale in your favor.

question: What divine wisdom did the Prophet ﷺ reveal regarding guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: أَوَّلُ مَا يُحَاسَبُ بِهِ الْعَبْدُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ مِنْ عَمَلِهِ صَلاَتُهُ
textEnglish: The first matter for which the slave of Allah will be brought to account on the Day of Judgment is his prayer.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 413, Sunan an-Nasa’i 465 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Salah is your personal appointment with the Lord of the worlds; safeguard its punctuality and focus.

question: How does consistent practice of guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّ الدِّينَ يُسْرٌ، وَلَنْ يُشَادَّ الدِّينَ أَحَدٌ إِلاَّ غَلَبَهُ
textEnglish: Indeed, the religion is easy, and no one makes the religion overly difficult except that it will overcome him.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 39 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Adopt a steady, balanced pace of devotion; moderation sustains lifelong spiritual growth.

question: What spiritual remedy does guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لَيْسَ الْغِنَى عَنْ كَثْرَةِ الْعَرَضِ، وَلَكِنَّ الْغِنَى غِنَى النَّفْسِ
textEnglish: Richness is not about abundance of worldly possessions; true wealth is the richness of contentment in the soul.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6446, Sahih Muslim 1051 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Peace is never found in endless material craving, but in tranquility and satisfaction with what Allah gave.

question: Why is sincere commitment to guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ فَلْيَقُلْ خَيْرًا أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ
textEnglish: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak what is beneficial or remain silent.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6018, Sahih Muslim 47 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Guarding speech protects relationships and preserves the dignity and purity of the heart.

question: How did the noble Companions embody guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَثَلُ الَّذِي يَذْكُرُ رَبَّهُ وَالَّذِي لاَ يَذْكُرُ رَبَّهُ مَثَلُ الْحَيِّ وَالْمَيِّتِ
textEnglish: The example of the one who remembers his Lord compared to the one who does not is like that of the living and the dead.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6407, Sahih Muslim 779 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Dhikr is the oxygen of the spiritual heart; without it, the inner being withers.

question: What warning or glad tiding is conveyed concerning guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَا يُصِيبُ الْمُسْلِمَ مِنْ نَصَبٍ وَلاَ وَصَبٍ وَلاَ هَمٍّ وَلاَ حَزَنٍ وَلاَ أَذًى حَتَّى الشَّوْكَةِ يُشَاكُهَا إِلاَّ كَفَّرَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مِنْ خَطَايَاهُ
textEnglish: No fatigue, illness, worry, grief, hurt, or distress befalls a believer—even the prick of a thorn—except that Allah expiates some of his sins through it.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5641, Sahih Muslim 2573 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Every silent patience during hardship is recognized, rewarded, and purified by the Most Merciful.

question: In what way does excellence in guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: تَبَسُّمُكَ فِي وَجْهِ أَخِيكَ لَكَ صَدَقَةٌ
textEnglish: Your smiling in the face of your brother is charity for you.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1956 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Radiating warmth and gentle kindness costs nothing yet carries eternal divine reward.

question: How can one safeguard guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الْمُسْلِمُ مَنْ سَلِمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِهِ وَيَدِهِ
textEnglish: The true Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hands other people are completely safe.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 10, Sahih Muslim 40 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Righteousness is verified when those around you live in safety from your harm and speech.

question: What essential principle transforms our approach to guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
textEnglish: The best among you are those who learn the Quran and teach it to others.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5027 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Connecting yourself with the Book of Allah and sharing its light with others is the pinnacle of nobility.

question: Why is genuine devotion in guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ سَلَكَ طَرِيقًا يَلْتَمِسُ فِيهِ عِلْمًا سَهَّلَ اللَّهُ لَهُ بِهِ طَرِيقًا إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ
textEnglish: Whoever travels a path seeking sacred knowledge, Allah makes smooth for him a path to Paradise.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2699 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Every moment dedicated to understanding faith and truth brings you closer to the gardens of Jannah.

textEnglish: Every one of you is a shepherd and guardian, and every one of you will be questioned concerning his flock.

textArabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ إِذَا عَمِلَ أَحَدُكُمْ عَمَلاً أَنْ يُتْقِنَهُ
textEnglish: Verily, Allah loves that whenever any of you undertakes a work, he executes it with mastery and excellence (Itqan).
reference: Shu’ab al-Iman (Al-Bayhaqi 4929, Hasan) · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Excellence in profession, study, and daily duty is an act of devotion loved by the Creator.

question: How can parents and mentors inspire guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الْحَيَاءُ لاَ يَأْتِي إِلاَّ بِخَيْرٍ
textEnglish: Modesty and conscience (Haya) bring nothing except goodness.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6117, Sahih Muslim 37 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Haya is a spiritual shield that restrains the soul from vulgarity and prompts noble conduct.

question: What guidance did the Prophet ﷺ emphasize regarding consistency in guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ كَفَلَ يَتِيمًا لَهُ أَوْ لِغَيْرِهِ فَأَنَا وَهُوَ كَهَاتَيْنِ فِي الْجَنَّةِ
textEnglish: The one who cares for an orphan and myself will be together in Paradise like these two fingers (joining his index and middle finger).
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5304, Sahih Muslim 2983 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Caring for vulnerable orphans guarantees the closest companionship with the Prophet ﷺ in the highest Jannah.

question: How does divine mercy embrace those who strive in guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَا نَقَصَتْ صَدَقَةٌ مِنْ مَالٍ، وَمَا زَادَ اللَّهُ عَبْدًا بِعَفْوٍ إِلاَّ عِزًّا
textEnglish: Charity never decreases wealth; and Allah never increases a servant who forgives except in honor and elevation.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2588 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Generosity and forgiveness never degrade a person; they invoke divine barakah and nobility.

question: In times of difficulty, how does guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: احْفَظِ اللَّهَ يَحْفَظْكَ، احْفَظِ اللَّهَ تَجِدْهُ تُجَاهَكَ
textEnglish: Be mindful of Allah, and He will protect you. Be mindful of Allah, and you will find Him facing you in every need.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2516 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Honor Allah’s commands in times of ease, and He will deliver and comfort you in times of adversity.

question: What reflection on the Hereafter is awakened by guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لَوْ أَنَّكُمْ تَوَكَّلُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ حَقَّ تَوَكُّلِهِ لَرَزَقَكُمْ كَمَا يَرْزُقُ الطَّيْرَ
textEnglish: If you were to rely upon Allah with true reliance (Tawakkul), He would provide for you just as He provides for birds: they depart hungry at dawn and return full at dusk.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2344, Sunan Ibn Majah 4164 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Combine practical effort with tranquil reliance upon the Ultimate Provider.

question: How does understanding guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: أَفْشُوا السَّلاَمَ، وَأَطْعِمُوا الطَّعَامَ، وَصِلُوا الأَرْحَامَ، وَصَلُّوا بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّاسُ نِيَامٌ، تَدْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ بِسَلاَمٍ
textEnglish: Spread peace (Salam), feed the hungry, maintain kinship ties, and pray during the night while people sleep: you will enter Paradise in complete peace.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2485, Sunan Ibn Majah 3251 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: The four golden keys to peaceful entry into Jannah unite communal kindness and private devotion.

question: What divine wisdom did the Prophet ﷺ reveal regarding guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الصَّدَقَةُ تَقَعُ فِي يَدِ الرَّحْمَنِ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَقَعَ فِي يَدِ السَّائِلِ
textEnglish: Charity falls into the Hand of the Most Merciful before it falls into the hand of the needy person.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1410, Sahih Muslim 1014 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Give charity with profound reverence; you are offering a direct transaction with your Lord.

question: How does consistent practice of guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الْمُؤْمِنُ الْقَوِيُّ خَيْرٌ وَأَحَبُّ إِلَى اللَّهِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِ الضَّعِيفِ، وَفِي كُلٍّ خَيْرٌ
textEnglish: The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, though there is goodness in both. Strive for what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not lose heart.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2664 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Cultivate mental, moral, physical, and spiritual strength while maintaining humble reliance on Allah.

question: What spiritual remedy does guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ سَرَّهُ أَنْ يُبْسَطَ لَهُ فِي رِزْقِهِ، وَأَنْ يُنْسَأَ لَهُ فِي أَثَرِهِ، فَلْيَصِلْ رَحِمَهُ
textEnglish: Whoever delights in having his provision expanded and his lifespan blessed and extended, let him maintain ties of kinship.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5986, Sahih Muslim 2557 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Kindness to relatives and family reconciliation draws barakah into time and livelihood.

question: Why is sincere commitment to guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِذَا مَاتَ الإِنْسَانُ انْقَطَعَ عَنْهُ عَمَلُهُ إِلاَّ مِنْ ثَلاَثَةٍ: صَدَقَةٍ جَارِيَةٍ، أَوْ عِلْمٍ يُنْتَفَعُ بِهِ، أَوْ وَلَدٍ صَالِحٍ يَدْعُو لَهُ
textEnglish: When a human being dies, all his deeds cease except for three: recurring charity (Sadaqah Jariyah), beneficial knowledge left behind, or a righteous child who prays for him.
reference: Sahih Muslim 1631 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Invest your life in legacies that continue to shine and generate divine rewards after your earthly departure.

question: How did the noble Companions embody guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّمَا الأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ، وَإِنَّمَا لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى
textEnglish: Actions are judged by motives and intentions, and every person will have only that which they intended.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1, Sahih Muslim 1907 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Purify your heart before every deed; a sincere intention transforms simple daily acts into perpetual worship.

question: What warning or glad tiding is conveyed concerning guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الإِيمَانُ أَنْ تُؤْمِنَ بِاللَّهِ، وَمَلاَئِكَتِهِ، وَكُتُبِهِ، وَرُسُلِهِ، وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ، وَتُؤْمِنَ بِالْقَدَرِ خَيْرِهِ وَشَرِّهِ
textEnglish: Faith is that you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and divine destiny—both its prosperity and adversity.
reference: Sahih Muslim 8 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Conviction in Allah’s wisdom gives the believer unwavering calm during life’s unpredictable changes.

question: In what way does excellence in guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الرَّاحِمُونَ يَرْحَمُهُمُ الرَّحْمَنُ، ارْحَمُوا مَنْ فِي الأَرْضِ يَرْحَمْكُمْ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاءِ
textEnglish: The merciful will be shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Be merciful to those on earth, and the One in the heavens will be merciful to you.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1924, Sunan Abi Dawud 4941 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Compassion to all living beings is the golden key that unlocks divine mercy and forgiveness.

question: How can one safeguard guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لاَ يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لأَخِيهِ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ
textEnglish: None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 13, Sahih Muslim 45 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Genuine faith cleanses the soul of jealousy and cultivates sincere goodwill toward all people.

question: What essential principle transforms our approach to guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّ مِنْ خِيَارِكُمْ أَحْسَنَكُمْ أَخْلاَقًا
textEnglish: Indeed, the best and most beloved among you are those who possess the best character and manners.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 3559, Sahih Muslim 2321 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Gentleness, integrity, and warmth of character are the true reflection of a living faith.

question: Why is genuine devotion in guarding the tongue from backbiting (gheebah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الطُّهُورُ شَطْرُ الإِيمَانِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ تَمْلأُ الْمِيزَانَ
textEnglish: Purity is half of faith, and “Alhamdulillah” (Praise be to Allah) fills the divine scale of deeds.
reference: Sahih Muslim 223 · Chapter 106: Guarding the Tongue from Backbiting (Gheebah)
keyLesson: Inner and outer purification are intertwined; heartfelt gratitude tilts the eternal scale in your favor.

question: What spiritual wisdom did the Prophet ﷺ teach regarding honoring promises & trusts (amanah)?

question: What eternal reward is promised for cultivating honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: أَوَّلُ مَا يُحَاسَبُ بِهِ الْعَبْدُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ مِنْ عَمَلِهِ صَلاَتُهُ
textEnglish: The first matter for which the slave of Allah will be brought to account on the Day of Judgment is his prayer.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 413, Sunan an-Nasa’i 465 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Salah is your personal appointment with the Lord of the worlds; safeguard its punctuality and focus.

question: How can parents and mentors inspire honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّ الدِّينَ يُسْرٌ، وَلَنْ يُشَادَّ الدِّينَ أَحَدٌ إِلاَّ غَلَبَهُ
textEnglish: Indeed, the religion is easy, and no one makes the religion overly difficult except that it will overcome him.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 39 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Adopt a steady, balanced pace of devotion; moderation sustains lifelong spiritual growth.

question: What guidance did the Prophet ﷺ emphasize regarding consistency in honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لَيْسَ الْغِنَى عَنْ كَثْرَةِ الْعَرَضِ، وَلَكِنَّ الْغِنَى غِنَى النَّفْسِ
textEnglish: Richness is not about abundance of worldly possessions; true wealth is the richness of contentment in the soul.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6446, Sahih Muslim 1051 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Peace is never found in endless material craving, but in tranquility and satisfaction with what Allah gave.

question: How does divine mercy embrace those who strive in honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ فَلْيَقُلْ خَيْرًا أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ
textEnglish: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak what is beneficial or remain silent.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6018, Sahih Muslim 47 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Guarding speech protects relationships and preserves the dignity and purity of the heart.

question: In times of difficulty, how does honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَثَلُ الَّذِي يَذْكُرُ رَبَّهُ وَالَّذِي لاَ يَذْكُرُ رَبَّهُ مَثَلُ الْحَيِّ وَالْمَيِّتِ
textEnglish: The example of the one who remembers his Lord compared to the one who does not is like that of the living and the dead.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6407, Sahih Muslim 779 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Dhikr is the oxygen of the spiritual heart; without it, the inner being withers.

question: What reflection on the Hereafter is awakened by honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَا يُصِيبُ الْمُسْلِمَ مِنْ نَصَبٍ وَلاَ وَصَبٍ وَلاَ هَمٍّ وَلاَ حَزَنٍ وَلاَ أَذًى حَتَّى الشَّوْكَةِ يُشَاكُهَا إِلاَّ كَفَّرَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مِنْ خَطَايَاهُ
textEnglish: No fatigue, illness, worry, grief, hurt, or distress befalls a believer—even the prick of a thorn—except that Allah expiates some of his sins through it.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5641, Sahih Muslim 2573 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Every silent patience during hardship is recognized, rewarded, and purified by the Most Merciful.

question: How does understanding honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: تَبَسُّمُكَ فِي وَجْهِ أَخِيكَ لَكَ صَدَقَةٌ
textEnglish: Your smiling in the face of your brother is charity for you.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1956 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Radiating warmth and gentle kindness costs nothing yet carries eternal divine reward.

question: What divine wisdom did the Prophet ﷺ reveal regarding honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الْمُسْلِمُ مَنْ سَلِمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِهِ وَيَدِهِ
textEnglish: The true Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hands other people are completely safe.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 10, Sahih Muslim 40 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Righteousness is verified when those around you live in safety from your harm and speech.

question: How does consistent practice of honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
textEnglish: The best among you are those who learn the Quran and teach it to others.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5027 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Connecting yourself with the Book of Allah and sharing its light with others is the pinnacle of nobility.

question: What spiritual remedy does honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ سَلَكَ طَرِيقًا يَلْتَمِسُ فِيهِ عِلْمًا سَهَّلَ اللَّهُ لَهُ بِهِ طَرِيقًا إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ
textEnglish: Whoever travels a path seeking sacred knowledge, Allah makes smooth for him a path to Paradise.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2699 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Every moment dedicated to understanding faith and truth brings you closer to the gardens of Jannah.

question: Why is sincere commitment to honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لاَ تَغْضَبْ، فَرَدَّدَ مِرَارًا، قَالَ: لاَ تَغْضَبْ
textEnglish: A man said to the Prophet: “Advise me.” He said: “Do not become angry.” The man repeated his request several times, and each time he replied: “Do not become angry.”
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6116 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Mastery over impulsive anger preserves wisdom, protects relationships, and prevents regret.

question: How did the noble Companions embody honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: اتَّقِ اللَّهَ حَيْثُمَا كُنْتَ، وَأَتْبِعِ السَّيِّئَةَ الْحَسَنَةَ تَمْحُهَا، وَخَالِقِ النَّاسَ بِخُلُقٍ حَسَنٍ
textEnglish: Be mindful of Allah wherever you are; follow an evil deed with a good one and it will erase it; and treat people with beautiful character.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1987 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Live with God-consciousness in private and public, rapidly correct missteps, and be gracious to all.

question: What warning or glad tiding is conveyed concerning honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: كُلُّكُمْ رَاعٍ وَكُلُّكُمْ مَسْئُولٌ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهِ
textEnglish: Every one of you is a shepherd and guardian, and every one of you will be questioned concerning his flock.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 893, Sahih Muslim 1829 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Leadership is a sacred trust and responsibility of service, not privilege or authority.

question: In what way does excellence in honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ إِذَا عَمِلَ أَحَدُكُمْ عَمَلاً أَنْ يُتْقِنَهُ
textEnglish: Verily, Allah loves that whenever any of you undertakes a work, he executes it with mastery and excellence (Itqan).
reference: Shu’ab al-Iman (Al-Bayhaqi 4929, Hasan) · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Excellence in profession, study, and daily duty is an act of devotion loved by the Creator.

question: How can one safeguard honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الْحَيَاءُ لاَ يَأْتِي إِلاَّ بِخَيْرٍ
textEnglish: Modesty and conscience (Haya) bring nothing except goodness.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6117, Sahih Muslim 37 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Haya is a spiritual shield that restrains the soul from vulgarity and prompts noble conduct.

question: What essential principle transforms our approach to honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ كَفَلَ يَتِيمًا لَهُ أَوْ لِغَيْرِهِ فَأَنَا وَهُوَ كَهَاتَيْنِ فِي الْجَنَّةِ
textEnglish: The one who cares for an orphan and myself will be together in Paradise like these two fingers (joining his index and middle finger).
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5304, Sahih Muslim 2983 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Caring for vulnerable orphans guarantees the closest companionship with the Prophet ﷺ in the highest Jannah.

question: Why is genuine devotion in honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَا نَقَصَتْ صَدَقَةٌ مِنْ مَالٍ، وَمَا زَادَ اللَّهُ عَبْدًا بِعَفْوٍ إِلاَّ عِزًّا
textEnglish: Charity never decreases wealth; and Allah never increases a servant who forgives except in honor and elevation.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2588 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Generosity and forgiveness never degrade a person; they invoke divine barakah and nobility.

question: How does the heart find tranquility through honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: احْفَظِ اللَّهَ يَحْفَظْكَ، احْفَظِ اللَّهَ تَجِدْهُ تُجَاهَكَ
textEnglish: Be mindful of Allah, and He will protect you. Be mindful of Allah, and you will find Him facing you in every need.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2516 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Honor Allah’s commands in times of ease, and He will deliver and comfort you in times of adversity.

question: What common pitfall did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ warn about in honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لَوْ أَنَّكُمْ تَوَكَّلُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ حَقَّ تَوَكُّلِهِ لَرَزَقَكُمْ كَمَا يَرْزُقُ الطَّيْرَ
textEnglish: If you were to rely upon Allah with true reliance (Tawakkul), He would provide for you just as He provides for birds: they depart hungry at dawn and return full at dusk.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2344, Sunan Ibn Majah 4164 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Combine practical effort with tranquil reliance upon the Ultimate Provider.

question: How does moral beauty manifest through honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: أَفْشُوا السَّلاَمَ، وَأَطْعِمُوا الطَّعَامَ، وَصِلُوا الأَرْحَامَ، وَصَلُّوا بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّاسُ نِيَامٌ، تَدْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ بِسَلاَمٍ
textEnglish: Spread peace (Salam), feed the hungry, maintain kinship ties, and pray during the night while people sleep: you will enter Paradise in complete peace.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2485, Sunan Ibn Majah 3251 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: The four golden keys to peaceful entry into Jannah unite communal kindness and private devotion.

question: What eternal reward is promised for cultivating honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الصَّدَقَةُ تَقَعُ فِي يَدِ الرَّحْمَنِ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَقَعَ فِي يَدِ السَّائِلِ
textEnglish: Charity falls into the Hand of the Most Merciful before it falls into the hand of the needy person.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1410, Sahih Muslim 1014 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Give charity with profound reverence; you are offering a direct transaction with your Lord.

question: How can parents and mentors inspire honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الْمُؤْمِنُ الْقَوِيُّ خَيْرٌ وَأَحَبُّ إِلَى اللَّهِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِ الضَّعِيفِ، وَفِي كُلٍّ خَيْرٌ
textEnglish: The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, though there is goodness in both. Strive for what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not lose heart.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2664 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Cultivate mental, moral, physical, and spiritual strength while maintaining humble reliance on Allah.

question: What guidance did the Prophet ﷺ emphasize regarding consistency in honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ سَرَّهُ أَنْ يُبْسَطَ لَهُ فِي رِزْقِهِ، وَأَنْ يُنْسَأَ لَهُ فِي أَثَرِهِ، فَلْيَصِلْ رَحِمَهُ
textEnglish: Whoever delights in having his provision expanded and his lifespan blessed and extended, let him maintain ties of kinship.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5986, Sahih Muslim 2557 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Kindness to relatives and family reconciliation draws barakah into time and livelihood.

question: How does divine mercy embrace those who strive in honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِذَا مَاتَ الإِنْسَانُ انْقَطَعَ عَنْهُ عَمَلُهُ إِلاَّ مِنْ ثَلاَثَةٍ: صَدَقَةٍ جَارِيَةٍ، أَوْ عِلْمٍ يُنْتَفَعُ بِهِ، أَوْ وَلَدٍ صَالِحٍ يَدْعُو لَهُ
textEnglish: When a human being dies, all his deeds cease except for three: recurring charity (Sadaqah Jariyah), beneficial knowledge left behind, or a righteous child who prays for him.
reference: Sahih Muslim 1631 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Invest your life in legacies that continue to shine and generate divine rewards after your earthly departure.

question: In times of difficulty, how does honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّمَا الأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ، وَإِنَّمَا لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى
textEnglish: Actions are judged by motives and intentions, and every person will have only that which they intended.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1, Sahih Muslim 1907 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Purify your heart before every deed; a sincere intention transforms simple daily acts into perpetual worship.

question: What reflection on the Hereafter is awakened by honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الإِيمَانُ أَنْ تُؤْمِنَ بِاللَّهِ، وَمَلاَئِكَتِهِ، وَكُتُبِهِ، وَرُسُلِهِ، وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ، وَتُؤْمِنَ بِالْقَدَرِ خَيْرِهِ وَشَرِّهِ
textEnglish: Faith is that you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and divine destiny—both its prosperity and adversity.
reference: Sahih Muslim 8 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Conviction in Allah’s wisdom gives the believer unwavering calm during life’s unpredictable changes.

question: How does understanding honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الرَّاحِمُونَ يَرْحَمُهُمُ الرَّحْمَنُ، ارْحَمُوا مَنْ فِي الأَرْضِ يَرْحَمْكُمْ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاءِ
textEnglish: The merciful will be shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Be merciful to those on earth, and the One in the heavens will be merciful to you.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1924, Sunan Abi Dawud 4941 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Compassion to all living beings is the golden key that unlocks divine mercy and forgiveness.

question: What divine wisdom did the Prophet ﷺ reveal regarding honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لاَ يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لأَخِيهِ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ
textEnglish: None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 13, Sahih Muslim 45 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Genuine faith cleanses the soul of jealousy and cultivates sincere goodwill toward all people.

question: How does consistent practice of honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّ مِنْ خِيَارِكُمْ أَحْسَنَكُمْ أَخْلاَقًا
textEnglish: Indeed, the best and most beloved among you are those who possess the best character and manners.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 3559, Sahih Muslim 2321 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Gentleness, integrity, and warmth of character are the true reflection of a living faith.

question: What spiritual remedy does honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الطُّهُورُ شَطْرُ الإِيمَانِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ تَمْلأُ الْمِيزَانَ
textEnglish: Purity is half of faith, and “Alhamdulillah” (Praise be to Allah) fills the divine scale of deeds.
reference: Sahih Muslim 223 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Inner and outer purification are intertwined; heartfelt gratitude tilts the eternal scale in your favor.

question: Why is sincere commitment to honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: أَوَّلُ مَا يُحَاسَبُ بِهِ الْعَبْدُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ مِنْ عَمَلِهِ صَلاَتُهُ
textEnglish: The first matter for which the slave of Allah will be brought to account on the Day of Judgment is his prayer.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 413, Sunan an-Nasa’i 465 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Salah is your personal appointment with the Lord of the worlds; safeguard its punctuality and focus.

question: How did the noble Companions embody honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّ الدِّينَ يُسْرٌ، وَلَنْ يُشَادَّ الدِّينَ أَحَدٌ إِلاَّ غَلَبَهُ
textEnglish: Indeed, the religion is easy, and no one makes the religion overly difficult except that it will overcome him.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 39 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Adopt a steady, balanced pace of devotion; moderation sustains lifelong spiritual growth.

question: What warning or glad tiding is conveyed concerning honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لَيْسَ الْغِنَى عَنْ كَثْرَةِ الْعَرَضِ، وَلَكِنَّ الْغِنَى غِنَى النَّفْسِ
textEnglish: Richness is not about abundance of worldly possessions; true wealth is the richness of contentment in the soul.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6446, Sahih Muslim 1051 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Peace is never found in endless material craving, but in tranquility and satisfaction with what Allah gave.

question: In what way does excellence in honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ فَلْيَقُلْ خَيْرًا أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ
textEnglish: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak what is beneficial or remain silent.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6018, Sahih Muslim 47 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Guarding speech protects relationships and preserves the dignity and purity of the heart.

question: How can one safeguard honoring promises & trusts (amanah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَثَلُ الَّذِي يَذْكُرُ رَبَّهُ وَالَّذِي لاَ يَذْكُرُ رَبَّهُ مَثَلُ الْحَيِّ وَالْمَيِّتِ

reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1956 · Chapter 107: Honoring Promises & Trusts (Amanah)
keyLesson: Radiating warmth and gentle kindness costs nothing yet carries eternal divine reward.

textArabic: إِنَّمَا الأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ، وَإِنَّمَا لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى

question: How does consistent practice of generosity without extravagance and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
