textArabic: مَا يُصِيبُ الْمُسْلِمَ مِنْ نَصَبٍ وَلاَ وَصَبٍ وَلاَ هَمٍّ وَلاَ حَزَنٍ وَلاَ أَذًى حَتَّى الشَّوْكَةِ يُشَاكُهَا إِلاَّ كَفَّرَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مِنْ خَطَايَاهُ
textEnglish: No fatigue, illness, worry, grief, hurt, or distress befalls a believer—even the prick of a thorn—except that Allah expiates some of his sins through it.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5641, Sahih Muslim 2573 · Chapter 137: Avoiding Speculation & Excessive Ambiguity (Gharar)
keyLesson: Every silent patience during hardship is recognized, rewarded, and purified by the Most Merciful.

question: How does understanding avoiding speculation & excessive ambiguity (gharar) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: تَبَسُّمُكَ فِي وَجْهِ أَخِيكَ لَكَ صَدَقَةٌ
textEnglish: Your smiling in the face of your brother is charity for you.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1956 · Chapter 137: Avoiding Speculation & Excessive Ambiguity (Gharar)
keyLesson: Radiating warmth and gentle kindness costs nothing yet carries eternal divine reward.

question: What divine wisdom did the Prophet ﷺ reveal regarding avoiding speculation & excessive ambiguity (gharar) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الْمُسْلِمُ مَنْ سَلِمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِهِ وَيَدِهِ
textEnglish: The true Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hands other people are completely safe.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 10, Sahih Muslim 40 · Chapter 137: Avoiding Speculation & Excessive Ambiguity (Gharar)
keyLesson: Righteousness is verified when those around you live in safety from your harm and speech.

question: How does consistent practice of avoiding speculation & excessive ambiguity (gharar) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
textEnglish: The best among you are those who learn the Quran and teach it to others.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5027 · Chapter 137: Avoiding Speculation & Excessive Ambiguity (Gharar)
keyLesson: Connecting yourself with the Book of Allah and sharing its light with others is the pinnacle of nobility.

question: What spiritual remedy does avoiding speculation & excessive ambiguity (gharar) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ سَلَكَ طَرِيقًا يَلْتَمِسُ فِيهِ عِلْمًا سَهَّلَ اللَّهُ لَهُ بِهِ طَرِيقًا إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ
textEnglish: Whoever travels a path seeking sacred knowledge, Allah makes smooth for him a path to Paradise.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2699 · Chapter 137: Avoiding Speculation & Excessive Ambiguity (Gharar)
keyLesson: Every moment dedicated to understanding faith and truth brings you closer to the gardens of Jannah.

question: Why is sincere commitment to avoiding speculation & excessive ambiguity (gharar) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لاَ تَغْضَبْ، فَرَدَّدَ مِرَارًا، قَالَ: لاَ تَغْضَبْ
textEnglish: A man said to the Prophet: “Advise me.” He said: “Do not become angry.” The man repeated his request several times, and each time he replied: “Do not become angry.”
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6116 · Chapter 137: Avoiding Speculation & Excessive Ambiguity (Gharar)
keyLesson: Mastery over impulsive anger preserves wisdom, protects relationships, and prevents regret.

question: How did the noble Companions embody avoiding speculation & excessive ambiguity (gharar) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: اتَّقِ اللَّهَ حَيْثُمَا كُنْتَ، وَأَتْبِعِ السَّيِّئَةَ الْحَسَنَةَ تَمْحُهَا، وَخَالِقِ النَّاسَ بِخُلُقٍ حَسَنٍ
textEnglish: Be mindful of Allah wherever you are; follow an evil deed with a good one and it will erase it; and treat people with beautiful character.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1987 · Chapter 137: Avoiding Speculation & Excessive Ambiguity (Gharar)
keyLesson: Live with God-consciousness in private and public, rapidly correct missteps, and be gracious to all.

question: What warning or glad tiding is conveyed concerning avoiding speculation & excessive ambiguity (gharar) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: كُلُّكُمْ رَاعٍ وَكُلُّكُمْ مَسْئُولٌ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهِ
textEnglish: Every one of you is a shepherd and guardian, and every one of you will be questioned concerning his flock.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 893, Sahih Muslim 1829 · Chapter 137: Avoiding Speculation & Excessive Ambiguity (Gharar)
keyLesson: Leadership is a sacred trust and responsibility of service, not privilege or authority.

question: In what way does excellence in avoiding speculation & excessive ambiguity (gharar) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ إِذَا عَمِلَ أَحَدُكُمْ عَمَلاً أَنْ يُتْقِنَهُ
textEnglish: Verily, Allah loves that whenever any of you undertakes a work, he executes it with mastery and excellence (Itqan).
reference: Shu’ab al-Iman (Al-Bayhaqi 4929, Hasan) · Chapter 137: Avoiding Speculation & Excessive Ambiguity (Gharar)
keyLesson: Excellence in profession, study, and daily duty is an act of devotion loved by the Creator.

question: How can one safeguard avoiding speculation & excessive ambiguity (gharar) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الْحَيَاءُ لاَ يَأْتِي إِلاَّ بِخَيْرٍ
textEnglish: Modesty and conscience (Haya) bring nothing except goodness.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6117, Sahih Muslim 37 · Chapter 137: Avoiding Speculation & Excessive Ambiguity (Gharar)
keyLesson: Haya is a spiritual shield that restrains the soul from vulgarity and prompts noble conduct.

question: What essential principle transforms our approach to avoiding speculation & excessive ambiguity (gharar) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ كَفَلَ يَتِيمًا لَهُ أَوْ لِغَيْرِهِ فَأَنَا وَهُوَ كَهَاتَيْنِ فِي الْجَنَّةِ
textEnglish: The one who cares for an orphan and myself will be together in Paradise like these two fingers (joining his index and middle finger).
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5304, Sahih Muslim 2983 · Chapter 137: Avoiding Speculation & Excessive Ambiguity (Gharar)
keyLesson: Caring for vulnerable orphans guarantees the closest companionship with the Prophet ﷺ in the highest Jannah.

question: Why is genuine devotion in avoiding speculation & excessive ambiguity (gharar) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَا نَقَصَتْ صَدَقَةٌ مِنْ مَالٍ، وَمَا زَادَ اللَّهُ عَبْدًا بِعَفْوٍ إِلاَّ عِزًّا
textEnglish: Charity never decreases wealth; and Allah never increases a servant who forgives except in honor and elevation.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2588 · Chapter 137: Avoiding Speculation & Excessive Ambiguity (Gharar)
keyLesson: Generosity and forgiveness never degrade a person; they invoke divine barakah and nobility.

question: How does the heart find tranquility through avoiding speculation & excessive ambiguity (gharar) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: احْفَظِ اللَّهَ يَحْفَظْكَ، احْفَظِ اللَّهَ تَجِدْهُ تُجَاهَكَ
textEnglish: Be mindful of Allah, and He will protect you. Be mindful of Allah, and you will find Him facing you in every need.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2516 · Chapter 137: Avoiding Speculation & Excessive Ambiguity (Gharar)
keyLesson: Honor Allah’s commands in times of ease, and He will deliver and comfort you in times of adversity.

question: What common pitfall did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ warn about in avoiding speculation & excessive ambiguity (gharar) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لَوْ أَنَّكُمْ تَوَكَّلُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ حَقَّ تَوَكُّلِهِ لَرَزَقَكُمْ كَمَا يَرْزُقُ الطَّيْرَ
textEnglish: If you were to rely upon Allah with true reliance (Tawakkul), He would provide for you just as He provides for birds: they depart hungry at dawn and return full at dusk.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2344, Sunan Ibn Majah 4164 · Chapter 137: Avoiding Speculation & Excessive Ambiguity (Gharar)
keyLesson: Combine practical effort with tranquil reliance upon the Ultimate Provider.

question: How does moral beauty manifest through avoiding speculation & excessive ambiguity (gharar) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: أَفْشُوا السَّلاَمَ، وَأَطْعِمُوا الطَّعَامَ، وَصِلُوا الأَرْحَامَ، وَصَلُّوا بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّاسُ نِيَامٌ، تَدْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ بِسَلاَمٍ
textEnglish: Spread peace (Salam), feed the hungry, maintain kinship ties, and pray during the night while people sleep: you will enter Paradise in complete peace.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2485, Sunan Ibn Majah 3251 · Chapter 137: Avoiding Speculation & Excessive Ambiguity (Gharar)
keyLesson: The four golden keys to peaceful entry into Jannah unite communal kindness and private devotion.

question: What eternal reward is promised for cultivating avoiding speculation & excessive ambiguity (gharar) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الصَّدَقَةُ تَقَعُ فِي يَدِ الرَّحْمَنِ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَقَعَ فِي يَدِ السَّائِلِ
textEnglish: Charity falls into the Hand of the Most Merciful before it falls into the hand of the needy person.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1410, Sahih Muslim 1014 · Chapter 137: Avoiding Speculation & Excessive Ambiguity (Gharar)
keyLesson: Give charity with profound reverence; you are offering a direct transaction with your Lord.

question: How can parents and mentors inspire avoiding speculation & excessive ambiguity (gharar) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الْمُؤْمِنُ الْقَوِيُّ خَيْرٌ وَأَحَبُّ إِلَى اللَّهِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِ الضَّعِيفِ، وَفِي كُلٍّ خَيْرٌ
textEnglish: The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, though there is goodness in both. Strive for what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not lose heart.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2664 · Chapter 137: Avoiding Speculation & Excessive Ambiguity (Gharar)
keyLesson: Cultivate mental, moral, physical, and spiritual strength while maintaining humble reliance on Allah.

question: What guidance did the Prophet ﷺ emphasize regarding consistency in avoiding speculation & excessive ambiguity (gharar) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ سَرَّهُ أَنْ يُبْسَطَ لَهُ فِي رِزْقِهِ، وَأَنْ يُنْسَأَ لَهُ فِي أَثَرِهِ، فَلْيَصِلْ رَحِمَهُ
textEnglish: Whoever delights in having his provision expanded and his lifespan blessed and extended, let him maintain ties of kinship.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5986, Sahih Muslim 2557 · Chapter 137: Avoiding Speculation & Excessive Ambiguity (Gharar)
keyLesson: Kindness to relatives and family reconciliation draws barakah into time and livelihood.

question: How does divine mercy embrace those who strive in avoiding speculation & excessive ambiguity (gharar) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِذَا مَاتَ الإِنْسَانُ انْقَطَعَ عَنْهُ عَمَلُهُ إِلاَّ مِنْ ثَلاَثَةٍ: صَدَقَةٍ جَارِيَةٍ، أَوْ عِلْمٍ يُنْتَفَعُ بِهِ، أَوْ وَلَدٍ صَالِحٍ يَدْعُو لَهُ
textEnglish: When a human being dies, all his deeds cease except for three: recurring charity (Sadaqah Jariyah), beneficial knowledge left behind, or a righteous child who prays for him.
reference: Sahih Muslim 1631 · Chapter 137: Avoiding Speculation & Excessive Ambiguity (Gharar)
keyLesson: Invest your life in legacies that continue to shine and generate divine rewards after your earthly departure.

question: In times of difficulty, how does avoiding speculation & excessive ambiguity (gharar) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّمَا الأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ، وَإِنَّمَا لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى
textEnglish: Actions are judged by motives and intentions, and every person will have only that which they intended.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1, Sahih Muslim 1907 · Chapter 137: Avoiding Speculation & Excessive Ambiguity (Gharar)
keyLesson: Purify your heart before every deed; a sincere intention transforms simple daily acts into perpetual worship.

question: What reflection on the Hereafter is awakened by avoiding speculation & excessive ambiguity (gharar) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الإِيمَانُ أَنْ تُؤْمِنَ بِاللَّهِ، وَمَلاَئِكَتِهِ، وَكُتُبِهِ، وَرُسُلِهِ، وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ، وَتُؤْمِنَ بِالْقَدَرِ خَيْرِهِ وَشَرِّهِ
textEnglish: Faith is that you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and divine destiny—both its prosperity and adversity.
reference: Sahih Muslim 8 · Chapter 137: Avoiding Speculation & Excessive Ambiguity (Gharar)
keyLesson: Conviction in Allah’s wisdom gives the believer unwavering calm during life’s unpredictable changes.

question: How does understanding avoiding speculation & excessive ambiguity (gharar) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الرَّاحِمُونَ يَرْحَمُهُمُ الرَّحْمَنُ، ارْحَمُوا مَنْ فِي الأَرْضِ يَرْحَمْكُمْ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاءِ
textEnglish: The merciful will be shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Be merciful to those on earth, and the One in the heavens will be merciful to you.

keyLesson: Compassion to all living beings is the golden key that unlocks divine mercy and forgiveness.

textArabic: لاَ يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لأَخِيهِ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ
textEnglish: None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 13, Sahih Muslim 45 · Chapter 137: Avoiding Speculation & Excessive Ambiguity (Gharar)
keyLesson: Genuine faith cleanses the soul of jealousy and cultivates sincere goodwill toward all people.

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 3559, Sahih Muslim 2321 · Chapter 137: Avoiding Speculation & Excessive Ambiguity (Gharar)
keyLesson: Gentleness, integrity, and warmth of character are the true reflection of a living faith.

question: What spiritual remedy does avoiding speculation & excessive ambiguity (gharar) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الطُّهُورُ شَطْرُ الإِيمَانِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ تَمْلأُ الْمِيزَانَ
textEnglish: Purity is half of faith, and “Alhamdulillah” (Praise be to Allah) fills the divine scale of deeds.
reference: Sahih Muslim 223 · Chapter 137: Avoiding Speculation & Excessive Ambiguity (Gharar)
keyLesson: Inner and outer purification are intertwined; heartfelt gratitude tilts the eternal scale in your favor.

question: Why is sincere commitment to avoiding speculation & excessive ambiguity (gharar) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: أَوَّلُ مَا يُحَاسَبُ بِهِ الْعَبْدُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ مِنْ عَمَلِهِ صَلاَتُهُ
textEnglish: The first matter for which the slave of Allah will be brought to account on the Day of Judgment is his prayer.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 413, Sunan an-Nasa’i 465 · Chapter 137: Avoiding Speculation & Excessive Ambiguity (Gharar)
keyLesson: Salah is your personal appointment with the Lord of the worlds; safeguard its punctuality and focus.

question: How did the noble Companions embody avoiding speculation & excessive ambiguity (gharar) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّ الدِّينَ يُسْرٌ، وَلَنْ يُشَادَّ الدِّينَ أَحَدٌ إِلاَّ غَلَبَهُ
textEnglish: Indeed, the religion is easy, and no one makes the religion overly difficult except that it will overcome him.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 39 · Chapter 137: Avoiding Speculation & Excessive Ambiguity (Gharar)
keyLesson: Adopt a steady, balanced pace of devotion; moderation sustains lifelong spiritual growth.

question: What essential principle transforms our approach to honoring partnerships and joint ventures and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لَيْسَ الْغِنَى عَنْ كَثْرَةِ الْعَرَضِ، وَلَكِنَّ الْغِنَى غِنَى النَّفْسِ
textEnglish: Richness is not about abundance of worldly possessions; true wealth is the richness of contentment in the soul.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6446, Sahih Muslim 1051 · Chapter 138: Honoring Partnerships and Joint Ventures
keyLesson: Peace is never found in endless material craving, but in tranquility and satisfaction with what Allah gave.

question: Why is genuine devotion in honoring partnerships and joint ventures and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ فَلْيَقُلْ خَيْرًا أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ
textEnglish: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak what is beneficial or remain silent.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6018, Sahih Muslim 47 · Chapter 138: Honoring Partnerships and Joint Ventures
keyLesson: Guarding speech protects relationships and preserves the dignity and purity of the heart.

question: How does the heart find tranquility through honoring partnerships and joint ventures and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَثَلُ الَّذِي يَذْكُرُ رَبَّهُ وَالَّذِي لاَ يَذْكُرُ رَبَّهُ مَثَلُ الْحَيِّ وَالْمَيِّتِ
textEnglish: The example of the one who remembers his Lord compared to the one who does not is like that of the living and the dead.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6407, Sahih Muslim 779 · Chapter 138: Honoring Partnerships and Joint Ventures
keyLesson: Dhikr is the oxygen of the spiritual heart; without it, the inner being withers.

question: What common pitfall did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ warn about in honoring partnerships and joint ventures and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَا يُصِيبُ الْمُسْلِمَ مِنْ نَصَبٍ وَلاَ وَصَبٍ وَلاَ هَمٍّ وَلاَ حَزَنٍ وَلاَ أَذًى حَتَّى الشَّوْكَةِ يُشَاكُهَا إِلاَّ كَفَّرَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مِنْ خَطَايَاهُ
textEnglish: No fatigue, illness, worry, grief, hurt, or distress befalls a believer—even the prick of a thorn—except that Allah expiates some of his sins through it.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5641, Sahih Muslim 2573 · Chapter 138: Honoring Partnerships and Joint Ventures
keyLesson: Every silent patience during hardship is recognized, rewarded, and purified by the Most Merciful.

question: How does moral beauty manifest through honoring partnerships and joint ventures and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: تَبَسُّمُكَ فِي وَجْهِ أَخِيكَ لَكَ صَدَقَةٌ
textEnglish: Your smiling in the face of your brother is charity for you.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1956 · Chapter 138: Honoring Partnerships and Joint Ventures
keyLesson: Radiating warmth and gentle kindness costs nothing yet carries eternal divine reward.

question: What eternal reward is promised for cultivating honoring partnerships and joint ventures and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الْمُسْلِمُ مَنْ سَلِمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِهِ وَيَدِهِ
textEnglish: The true Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hands other people are completely safe.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 10, Sahih Muslim 40 · Chapter 138: Honoring Partnerships and Joint Ventures
keyLesson: Righteousness is verified when those around you live in safety from your harm and speech.

question: How can parents and mentors inspire honoring partnerships and joint ventures and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
textEnglish: The best among you are those who learn the Quran and teach it to others.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5027 · Chapter 138: Honoring Partnerships and Joint Ventures
keyLesson: Connecting yourself with the Book of Allah and sharing its light with others is the pinnacle of nobility.

question: What guidance did the Prophet ﷺ emphasize regarding consistency in honoring partnerships and joint ventures and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ سَلَكَ طَرِيقًا يَلْتَمِسُ فِيهِ عِلْمًا سَهَّلَ اللَّهُ لَهُ بِهِ طَرِيقًا إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ
textEnglish: Whoever travels a path seeking sacred knowledge, Allah makes smooth for him a path to Paradise.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2699 · Chapter 138: Honoring Partnerships and Joint Ventures
keyLesson: Every moment dedicated to understanding faith and truth brings you closer to the gardens of Jannah.

question: How does divine mercy embrace those who strive in honoring partnerships and joint ventures and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لاَ تَغْضَبْ، فَرَدَّدَ مِرَارًا، قَالَ: لاَ تَغْضَبْ
textEnglish: A man said to the Prophet: “Advise me.” He said: “Do not become angry.” The man repeated his request several times, and each time he replied: “Do not become angry.”
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6116 · Chapter 138: Honoring Partnerships and Joint Ventures
keyLesson: Mastery over impulsive anger preserves wisdom, protects relationships, and prevents regret.

question: In times of difficulty, how does honoring partnerships and joint ventures and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: اتَّقِ اللَّهَ حَيْثُمَا كُنْتَ، وَأَتْبِعِ السَّيِّئَةَ الْحَسَنَةَ تَمْحُهَا، وَخَالِقِ النَّاسَ بِخُلُقٍ حَسَنٍ
textEnglish: Be mindful of Allah wherever you are; follow an evil deed with a good one and it will erase it; and treat people with beautiful character.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1987 · Chapter 138: Honoring Partnerships and Joint Ventures
keyLesson: Live with God-consciousness in private and public, rapidly correct missteps, and be gracious to all.

question: What reflection on the Hereafter is awakened by honoring partnerships and joint ventures and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: كُلُّكُمْ رَاعٍ وَكُلُّكُمْ مَسْئُولٌ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهِ
textEnglish: Every one of you is a shepherd and guardian, and every one of you will be questioned concerning his flock.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 893, Sahih Muslim 1829 · Chapter 138: Honoring Partnerships and Joint Ventures
keyLesson: Leadership is a sacred trust and responsibility of service, not privilege or authority.

question: How does understanding honoring partnerships and joint ventures and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ إِذَا عَمِلَ أَحَدُكُمْ عَمَلاً أَنْ يُتْقِنَهُ
textEnglish: Verily, Allah loves that whenever any of you undertakes a work, he executes it with mastery and excellence (Itqan).
reference: Shu’ab al-Iman (Al-Bayhaqi 4929, Hasan) · Chapter 138: Honoring Partnerships and Joint Ventures
keyLesson: Excellence in profession, study, and daily duty is an act of devotion loved by the Creator.

question: What divine wisdom did the Prophet ﷺ reveal regarding honoring partnerships and joint ventures and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الْحَيَاءُ لاَ يَأْتِي إِلاَّ بِخَيْرٍ
textEnglish: Modesty and conscience (Haya) bring nothing except goodness.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6117, Sahih Muslim 37 · Chapter 138: Honoring Partnerships and Joint Ventures
keyLesson: Haya is a spiritual shield that restrains the soul from vulgarity and prompts noble conduct.

question: How does consistent practice of honoring partnerships and joint ventures and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ كَفَلَ يَتِيمًا لَهُ أَوْ لِغَيْرِهِ فَأَنَا وَهُوَ كَهَاتَيْنِ فِي الْجَنَّةِ
textEnglish: The one who cares for an orphan and myself will be together in Paradise like these two fingers (joining his index and middle finger).
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5304, Sahih Muslim 2983 · Chapter 138: Honoring Partnerships and Joint Ventures
keyLesson: Caring for vulnerable orphans guarantees the closest companionship with the Prophet ﷺ in the highest Jannah.

textArabic: مَا نَقَصَتْ صَدَقَةٌ مِنْ مَالٍ، وَمَا زَادَ اللَّهُ عَبْدًا بِعَفْوٍ إِلاَّ عِزًّا
textEnglish: Charity never decreases wealth; and Allah never increases a servant who forgives except in honor and elevation.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2588 · Chapter 138: Honoring Partnerships and Joint Ventures
keyLesson: Generosity and forgiveness never degrade a person; they invoke divine barakah and nobility.

question: Why is sincere commitment to honoring partnerships and joint ventures and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: احْفَظِ اللَّهَ يَحْفَظْكَ، احْفَظِ اللَّهَ تَجِدْهُ تُجَاهَكَ
textEnglish: Be mindful of Allah, and He will protect you. Be mindful of Allah, and you will find Him facing you in every need.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2516 · Chapter 138: Honoring Partnerships and Joint Ventures
keyLesson: Honor Allah’s commands in times of ease, and He will deliver and comfort you in times of adversity.

question: How did the noble Companions embody honoring partnerships and joint ventures and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لَوْ أَنَّكُمْ تَوَكَّلُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ حَقَّ تَوَكُّلِهِ لَرَزَقَكُمْ كَمَا يَرْزُقُ الطَّيْرَ
textEnglish: If you were to rely upon Allah with true reliance (Tawakkul), He would provide for you just as He provides for birds: they depart hungry at dawn and return full at dusk.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2344, Sunan Ibn Majah 4164 · Chapter 138: Honoring Partnerships and Joint Ventures
keyLesson: Combine practical effort with tranquil reliance upon the Ultimate Provider.

question: What warning or glad tiding is conveyed concerning honoring partnerships and joint ventures and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: أَفْشُوا السَّلاَمَ، وَأَطْعِمُوا الطَّعَامَ، وَصِلُوا الأَرْحَامَ، وَصَلُّوا بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّاسُ نِيَامٌ، تَدْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ بِسَلاَمٍ
textEnglish: Spread peace (Salam), feed the hungry, maintain kinship ties, and pray during the night while people sleep: you will enter Paradise in complete peace.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2485, Sunan Ibn Majah 3251 · Chapter 138: Honoring Partnerships and Joint Ventures
keyLesson: The four golden keys to peaceful entry into Jannah unite communal kindness and private devotion.

question: In what way does excellence in honoring partnerships and joint ventures and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الصَّدَقَةُ تَقَعُ فِي يَدِ الرَّحْمَنِ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَقَعَ فِي يَدِ السَّائِلِ
textEnglish: Charity falls into the Hand of the Most Merciful before it falls into the hand of the needy person.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1410, Sahih Muslim 1014 · Chapter 138: Honoring Partnerships and Joint Ventures
keyLesson: Give charity with profound reverence; you are offering a direct transaction with your Lord.

textArabic: الْمُؤْمِنُ الْقَوِيُّ خَيْرٌ وَأَحَبُّ إِلَى اللَّهِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِ الضَّعِيفِ، وَفِي كُلٍّ خَيْرٌ
textEnglish: The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, though there is goodness in both. Strive for what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not lose heart.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2664 · Chapter 138: Honoring Partnerships and Joint Ventures
keyLesson: Cultivate mental, moral, physical, and spiritual strength while maintaining humble reliance on Allah.

question: What essential principle transforms our approach to honoring partnerships and joint ventures and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ سَرَّهُ أَنْ يُبْسَطَ لَهُ فِي رِزْقِهِ، وَأَنْ يُنْسَأَ لَهُ فِي أَثَرِهِ، فَلْيَصِلْ رَحِمَهُ
textEnglish: Whoever delights in having his provision expanded and his lifespan blessed and extended, let him maintain ties of kinship.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5986, Sahih Muslim 2557 · Chapter 138: Honoring Partnerships and Joint Ventures
keyLesson: Kindness to relatives and family reconciliation draws barakah into time and livelihood.

question: Why is genuine devotion in honoring partnerships and joint ventures and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِذَا مَاتَ الإِنْسَانُ انْقَطَعَ عَنْهُ عَمَلُهُ إِلاَّ مِنْ ثَلاَثَةٍ: صَدَقَةٍ جَارِيَةٍ، أَوْ عِلْمٍ يُنْتَفَعُ بِهِ، أَوْ وَلَدٍ صَالِحٍ يَدْعُو لَهُ
textEnglish: When a human being dies, all his deeds cease except for three: recurring charity (Sadaqah Jariyah), beneficial knowledge left behind, or a righteous child who prays for him.
reference: Sahih Muslim 1631 · Chapter 138: Honoring Partnerships and Joint Ventures
keyLesson: Invest your life in legacies that continue to shine and generate divine rewards after your earthly departure.

keyLesson: Radiating warmth and gentle kindness costs nothing yet carries eternal divine reward.

keyLesson: Connecting yourself with the Book of Allah and sharing its light with others is the pinnacle of nobility.

keyLesson: Mastery over impulsive anger preserves wisdom, protects relationships, and prevents regret.

textEnglish: Be mindful of Allah wherever you are; follow an evil deed with a good one and it will erase it; and treat people with beautiful character.

keyLesson: Live with God-consciousness in private and public, rapidly correct missteps, and be gracious to all.

question: What essential principle transforms our approach to honoring partnerships and joint ventures and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: كُلُّكُمْ رَاعٍ وَكُلُّكُمْ مَسْئُولٌ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهِ
textEnglish: Every one of you is a shepherd and guardian, and every one of you will be questioned concerning his flock.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 893, Sahih Muslim 1829 · Chapter 138: Honoring Partnerships and Joint Ventures
keyLesson: Leadership is a sacred trust and responsibility of service, not privilege or authority.

textArabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ إِذَا عَمِلَ أَحَدُكُمْ عَمَلاً أَنْ يُتْقِنَهُ
textEnglish: Verily, Allah loves that whenever any of you undertakes a work, he executes it with mastery and excellence (Itqan).
reference: Shu’ab al-Iman (Al-Bayhaqi 4929, Hasan) · Chapter 138: Honoring Partnerships and Joint Ventures
keyLesson: Excellence in profession, study, and daily duty is an act of devotion loved by the Creator.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: What spiritual wisdom did the Prophet ﷺ teach regarding the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily?
textArabic: أَوَّلُ مَا يُحَاسَبُ بِهِ الْعَبْدُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ مِنْ عَمَلِهِ صَلاَتُهُ
textEnglish: The first matter for which the slave of Allah will be brought to account on the Day of Judgment is his prayer.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 413, Sunan an-Nasa’i 465 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Salah is your personal appointment with the Lord of the worlds; safeguard its punctuality and focus.

textEnglish: Indeed, the religion is easy, and no one makes the religion overly difficult except that it will overcome him.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 39 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily

textArabic: الْحَيَاءُ لاَ يَأْتِي إِلاَّ بِخَيْرٍ
textEnglish: Modesty and conscience (Haya) bring nothing except goodness.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6117, Sahih Muslim 37 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Haya is a spiritual shield that restrains the soul from vulgarity and prompts noble conduct.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: How can parents and mentors inspire the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ كَفَلَ يَتِيمًا لَهُ أَوْ لِغَيْرِهِ فَأَنَا وَهُوَ كَهَاتَيْنِ فِي الْجَنَّةِ
textEnglish: The one who cares for an orphan and myself will be together in Paradise like these two fingers (joining his index and middle finger).
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5304, Sahih Muslim 2983 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Caring for vulnerable orphans guarantees the closest companionship with the Prophet ﷺ in the highest Jannah.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: What guidance did the Prophet ﷺ emphasize regarding consistency in the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَا نَقَصَتْ صَدَقَةٌ مِنْ مَالٍ، وَمَا زَادَ اللَّهُ عَبْدًا بِعَفْوٍ إِلاَّ عِزًّا
textEnglish: Charity never decreases wealth; and Allah never increases a servant who forgives except in honor and elevation.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2588 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Generosity and forgiveness never degrade a person; they invoke divine barakah and nobility.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: How does divine mercy embrace those who strive in the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: احْفَظِ اللَّهَ يَحْفَظْكَ، احْفَظِ اللَّهَ تَجِدْهُ تُجَاهَكَ
textEnglish: Be mindful of Allah, and He will protect you. Be mindful of Allah, and you will find Him facing you in every need.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2516 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Honor Allah’s commands in times of ease, and He will deliver and comfort you in times of adversity.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: In times of difficulty, how does the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لَوْ أَنَّكُمْ تَوَكَّلُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ حَقَّ تَوَكُّلِهِ لَرَزَقَكُمْ كَمَا يَرْزُقُ الطَّيْرَ
textEnglish: If you were to rely upon Allah with true reliance (Tawakkul), He would provide for you just as He provides for birds: they depart hungry at dawn and return full at dusk.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2344, Sunan Ibn Majah 4164 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Combine practical effort with tranquil reliance upon the Ultimate Provider.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: What reflection on the Hereafter is awakened by the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: أَفْشُوا السَّلاَمَ، وَأَطْعِمُوا الطَّعَامَ، وَصِلُوا الأَرْحَامَ، وَصَلُّوا بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّاسُ نِيَامٌ، تَدْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ بِسَلاَمٍ
textEnglish: Spread peace (Salam), feed the hungry, maintain kinship ties, and pray during the night while people sleep: you will enter Paradise in complete peace.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2485, Sunan Ibn Majah 3251 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: The four golden keys to peaceful entry into Jannah unite communal kindness and private devotion.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: How does understanding the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الصَّدَقَةُ تَقَعُ فِي يَدِ الرَّحْمَنِ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَقَعَ فِي يَدِ السَّائِلِ
textEnglish: Charity falls into the Hand of the Most Merciful before it falls into the hand of the needy person.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1410, Sahih Muslim 1014 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Give charity with profound reverence; you are offering a direct transaction with your Lord.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: What divine wisdom did the Prophet ﷺ reveal regarding the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الْمُؤْمِنُ الْقَوِيُّ خَيْرٌ وَأَحَبُّ إِلَى اللَّهِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِ الضَّعِيفِ، وَفِي كُلٍّ خَيْرٌ
textEnglish: The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, though there is goodness in both. Strive for what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not lose heart.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2664 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Cultivate mental, moral, physical, and spiritual strength while maintaining humble reliance on Allah.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: How does consistent practice of the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ سَرَّهُ أَنْ يُبْسَطَ لَهُ فِي رِزْقِهِ، وَأَنْ يُنْسَأَ لَهُ فِي أَثَرِهِ، فَلْيَصِلْ رَحِمَهُ
textEnglish: Whoever delights in having his provision expanded and his lifespan blessed and extended, let him maintain ties of kinship.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5986, Sahih Muslim 2557 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Kindness to relatives and family reconciliation draws barakah into time and livelihood.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: What spiritual remedy does the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِذَا مَاتَ الإِنْسَانُ انْقَطَعَ عَنْهُ عَمَلُهُ إِلاَّ مِنْ ثَلاَثَةٍ: صَدَقَةٍ جَارِيَةٍ، أَوْ عِلْمٍ يُنْتَفَعُ بِهِ، أَوْ وَلَدٍ صَالِحٍ يَدْعُو لَهُ
textEnglish: When a human being dies, all his deeds cease except for three: recurring charity (Sadaqah Jariyah), beneficial knowledge left behind, or a righteous child who prays for him.
reference: Sahih Muslim 1631 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Invest your life in legacies that continue to shine and generate divine rewards after your earthly departure.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: Why is sincere commitment to the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّمَا الأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ، وَإِنَّمَا لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى
textEnglish: Actions are judged by motives and intentions, and every person will have only that which they intended.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1, Sahih Muslim 1907 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Purify your heart before every deed; a sincere intention transforms simple daily acts into perpetual worship.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: How did the noble Companions embody the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الإِيمَانُ أَنْ تُؤْمِنَ بِاللَّهِ، وَمَلاَئِكَتِهِ، وَكُتُبِهِ، وَرُسُلِهِ، وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ، وَتُؤْمِنَ بِالْقَدَرِ خَيْرِهِ وَشَرِّهِ
textEnglish: Faith is that you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and divine destiny—both its prosperity and adversity.
reference: Sahih Muslim 8 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Conviction in Allah’s wisdom gives the believer unwavering calm during life’s unpredictable changes.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: What warning or glad tiding is conveyed concerning the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الرَّاحِمُونَ يَرْحَمُهُمُ الرَّحْمَنُ، ارْحَمُوا مَنْ فِي الأَرْضِ يَرْحَمْكُمْ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاءِ
textEnglish: The merciful will be shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Be merciful to those on earth, and the One in the heavens will be merciful to you.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1924, Sunan Abi Dawud 4941 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Compassion to all living beings is the golden key that unlocks divine mercy and forgiveness.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: In what way does excellence in the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لاَ يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لأَخِيهِ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ
textEnglish: None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 13, Sahih Muslim 45 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Genuine faith cleanses the soul of jealousy and cultivates sincere goodwill toward all people.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: How can one safeguard the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّ مِنْ خِيَارِكُمْ أَحْسَنَكُمْ أَخْلاَقًا
textEnglish: Indeed, the best and most beloved among you are those who possess the best character and manners.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 3559, Sahih Muslim 2321 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Gentleness, integrity, and warmth of character are the true reflection of a living faith.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: What essential principle transforms our approach to the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الطُّهُورُ شَطْرُ الإِيمَانِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ تَمْلأُ الْمِيزَانَ
textEnglish: Purity is half of faith, and “Alhamdulillah” (Praise be to Allah) fills the divine scale of deeds.
reference: Sahih Muslim 223 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Inner and outer purification are intertwined; heartfelt gratitude tilts the eternal scale in your favor.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: Why is genuine devotion in the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: أَوَّلُ مَا يُحَاسَبُ بِهِ الْعَبْدُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ مِنْ عَمَلِهِ صَلاَتُهُ
textEnglish: The first matter for which the slave of Allah will be brought to account on the Day of Judgment is his prayer.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 413, Sunan an-Nasa’i 465 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Salah is your personal appointment with the Lord of the worlds; safeguard its punctuality and focus.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: How does the heart find tranquility through the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّ الدِّينَ يُسْرٌ، وَلَنْ يُشَادَّ الدِّينَ أَحَدٌ إِلاَّ غَلَبَهُ
textEnglish: Indeed, the religion is easy, and no one makes the religion overly difficult except that it will overcome him.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 39 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Adopt a steady, balanced pace of devotion; moderation sustains lifelong spiritual growth.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: What common pitfall did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ warn about in the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لَيْسَ الْغِنَى عَنْ كَثْرَةِ الْعَرَضِ، وَلَكِنَّ الْغِنَى غِنَى النَّفْسِ
textEnglish: Richness is not about abundance of worldly possessions; true wealth is the richness of contentment in the soul.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6446, Sahih Muslim 1051 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Peace is never found in endless material craving, but in tranquility and satisfaction with what Allah gave.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: How does moral beauty manifest through the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ فَلْيَقُلْ خَيْرًا أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ
textEnglish: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak what is beneficial or remain silent.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6018, Sahih Muslim 47 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Guarding speech protects relationships and preserves the dignity and purity of the heart.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: What eternal reward is promised for cultivating the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَثَلُ الَّذِي يَذْكُرُ رَبَّهُ وَالَّذِي لاَ يَذْكُرُ رَبَّهُ مَثَلُ الْحَيِّ وَالْمَيِّتِ
textEnglish: The example of the one who remembers his Lord compared to the one who does not is like that of the living and the dead.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6407, Sahih Muslim 779 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Dhikr is the oxygen of the spiritual heart; without it, the inner being withers.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: How can parents and mentors inspire the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَا يُصِيبُ الْمُسْلِمَ مِنْ نَصَبٍ وَلاَ وَصَبٍ وَلاَ هَمٍّ وَلاَ حَزَنٍ وَلاَ أَذًى حَتَّى الشَّوْكَةِ يُشَاكُهَا إِلاَّ كَفَّرَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مِنْ خَطَايَاهُ
textEnglish: No fatigue, illness, worry, grief, hurt, or distress befalls a believer—even the prick of a thorn—except that Allah expiates some of his sins through it.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5641, Sahih Muslim 2573 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Every silent patience during hardship is recognized, rewarded, and purified by the Most Merciful.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: What guidance did the Prophet ﷺ emphasize regarding consistency in the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: تَبَسُّمُكَ فِي وَجْهِ أَخِيكَ لَكَ صَدَقَةٌ
textEnglish: Your smiling in the face of your brother is charity for you.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1956 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Radiating warmth and gentle kindness costs nothing yet carries eternal divine reward.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: How does divine mercy embrace those who strive in the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الْمُسْلِمُ مَنْ سَلِمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِهِ وَيَدِهِ
textEnglish: The true Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hands other people are completely safe.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 10, Sahih Muslim 40 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Righteousness is verified when those around you live in safety from your harm and speech.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: In times of difficulty, how does the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
textEnglish: The best among you are those who learn the Quran and teach it to others.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5027 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Connecting yourself with the Book of Allah and sharing its light with others is the pinnacle of nobility.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: What reflection on the Hereafter is awakened by the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ سَلَكَ طَرِيقًا يَلْتَمِسُ فِيهِ عِلْمًا سَهَّلَ اللَّهُ لَهُ بِهِ طَرِيقًا إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ
textEnglish: Whoever travels a path seeking sacred knowledge, Allah makes smooth for him a path to Paradise.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2699 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Every moment dedicated to understanding faith and truth brings you closer to the gardens of Jannah.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: How does understanding the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لاَ تَغْضَبْ، فَرَدَّدَ مِرَارًا، قَالَ: لاَ تَغْضَبْ
textEnglish: A man said to the Prophet: “Advise me.” He said: “Do not become angry.” The man repeated his request several times, and each time he replied: “Do not become angry.”
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6116 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Mastery over impulsive anger preserves wisdom, protects relationships, and prevents regret.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: What divine wisdom did the Prophet ﷺ reveal regarding the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: اتَّقِ اللَّهَ حَيْثُمَا كُنْتَ، وَأَتْبِعِ السَّيِّئَةَ الْحَسَنَةَ تَمْحُهَا، وَخَالِقِ النَّاسَ بِخُلُقٍ حَسَنٍ
textEnglish: Be mindful of Allah wherever you are; follow an evil deed with a good one and it will erase it; and treat people with beautiful character.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1987 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Live with God-consciousness in private and public, rapidly correct missteps, and be gracious to all.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: How does consistent practice of the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: كُلُّكُمْ رَاعٍ وَكُلُّكُمْ مَسْئُولٌ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهِ
textEnglish: Every one of you is a shepherd and guardian, and every one of you will be questioned concerning his flock.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 893, Sahih Muslim 1829 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Leadership is a sacred trust and responsibility of service, not privilege or authority.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: What spiritual remedy does the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ إِذَا عَمِلَ أَحَدُكُمْ عَمَلاً أَنْ يُتْقِنَهُ
textEnglish: Verily, Allah loves that whenever any of you undertakes a work, he executes it with mastery and excellence (Itqan).
reference: Shu’ab al-Iman (Al-Bayhaqi 4929, Hasan) · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Excellence in profession, study, and daily duty is an act of devotion loved by the Creator.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: Why is sincere commitment to the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الْحَيَاءُ لاَ يَأْتِي إِلاَّ بِخَيْرٍ
textEnglish: Modesty and conscience (Haya) bring nothing except goodness.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6117, Sahih Muslim 37 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Haya is a spiritual shield that restrains the soul from vulgarity and prompts noble conduct.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: How did the noble Companions embody the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ كَفَلَ يَتِيمًا لَهُ أَوْ لِغَيْرِهِ فَأَنَا وَهُوَ كَهَاتَيْنِ فِي الْجَنَّةِ
textEnglish: The one who cares for an orphan and myself will be together in Paradise like these two fingers (joining his index and middle finger).
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5304, Sahih Muslim 2983 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Caring for vulnerable orphans guarantees the closest companionship with the Prophet ﷺ in the highest Jannah.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: What warning or glad tiding is conveyed concerning the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَا نَقَصَتْ صَدَقَةٌ مِنْ مَالٍ، وَمَا زَادَ اللَّهُ عَبْدًا بِعَفْوٍ إِلاَّ عِزًّا
textEnglish: Charity never decreases wealth; and Allah never increases a servant who forgives except in honor and elevation.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2588 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Generosity and forgiveness never degrade a person; they invoke divine barakah and nobility.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: In what way does excellence in the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: احْفَظِ اللَّهَ يَحْفَظْكَ، احْفَظِ اللَّهَ تَجِدْهُ تُجَاهَكَ
textEnglish: Be mindful of Allah, and He will protect you. Be mindful of Allah, and you will find Him facing you in every need.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2516 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Honor Allah’s commands in times of ease, and He will deliver and comfort you in times of adversity.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: How can one safeguard the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لَوْ أَنَّكُمْ تَوَكَّلُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ حَقَّ تَوَكُّلِهِ لَرَزَقَكُمْ كَمَا يَرْزُقُ الطَّيْرَ
textEnglish: If you were to rely upon Allah with true reliance (Tawakkul), He would provide for you just as He provides for birds: they depart hungry at dawn and return full at dusk.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2344, Sunan Ibn Majah 4164 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Combine practical effort with tranquil reliance upon the Ultimate Provider.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: What essential principle transforms our approach to the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: أَفْشُوا السَّلاَمَ، وَأَطْعِمُوا الطَّعَامَ، وَصِلُوا الأَرْحَامَ، وَصَلُّوا بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّاسُ نِيَامٌ، تَدْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ بِسَلاَمٍ
textEnglish: Spread peace (Salam), feed the hungry, maintain kinship ties, and pray during the night while people sleep: you will enter Paradise in complete peace.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2485, Sunan Ibn Majah 3251 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: The four golden keys to peaceful entry into Jannah unite communal kindness and private devotion.

subTopicTitle: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
question: Why is genuine devotion in the danger of defaulting on debts voluntarily and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الصَّدَقَةُ تَقَعُ فِي يَدِ الرَّحْمَنِ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَقَعَ فِي يَدِ السَّائِلِ
textEnglish: Charity falls into the Hand of the Most Merciful before it falls into the hand of the needy person.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1410, Sahih Muslim 1014 · Chapter 139: The Danger of Defaulting on Debts Voluntarily
keyLesson: Give charity with profound reverence; you are offering a direct transaction with your Lord.

textArabic: مَا نَقَصَتْ صَدَقَةٌ مِنْ مَالٍ، وَمَا زَادَ اللَّهُ عَبْدًا بِعَفْوٍ إِلاَّ عِزًّا

reference: Sahih Muslim 2588 · Chapter 140: Endowments & Sustainable Awqaf
keyLesson: Generosity and forgiveness never degrade a person; they invoke divine barakah and nobility.

textArabic: احْفَظِ اللَّهَ يَحْفَظْكَ، احْفَظِ اللَّهَ تَجِدْهُ تُجَاهَكَ
textEnglish: Be mindful of Allah, and He will protect you. Be mindful of Allah, and you will find Him facing you in every need.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2516 · Chapter 140: Endowments & Sustainable Awqaf
keyLesson: Honor Allah’s commands in times of ease, and He will deliver and comfort you in times of adversity.

question: How does the heart find tranquility through endowments & sustainable awqaf and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لَوْ أَنَّكُمْ تَوَكَّلُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ حَقَّ تَوَكُّلِهِ لَرَزَقَكُمْ كَمَا يَرْزُقُ الطَّيْرَ
textEnglish: If you were to rely upon Allah with true reliance (Tawakkul), He would provide for you just as He provides for birds: they depart hungry at dawn and return full at dusk.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2344, Sunan Ibn Majah 4164 · Chapter 140: Endowments & Sustainable Awqaf
keyLesson: Combine practical effort with tranquil reliance upon the Ultimate Provider.

keyLesson: The four golden keys to peaceful entry into Jannah unite communal kindness and private devotion.

reference: Sahih Muslim 2664 · Chapter 140: Endowments & Sustainable Awqaf
keyLesson: Cultivate mental, moral, physical, and spiritual strength while maintaining humble reliance on Allah.

question: How can parents and mentors inspire endowments & sustainable awqaf and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ سَرَّهُ أَنْ يُبْسَطَ لَهُ فِي رِزْقِهِ، وَأَنْ يُنْسَأَ لَهُ فِي أَثَرِهِ، فَلْيَصِلْ رَحِمَهُ
textEnglish: Whoever delights in having his provision expanded and his lifespan blessed and extended, let him maintain ties of kinship.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5986, Sahih Muslim 2557 · Chapter 140: Endowments & Sustainable Awqaf
keyLesson: Kindness to relatives and family reconciliation draws barakah into time and livelihood.

question: What guidance did the Prophet ﷺ emphasize regarding consistency in endowments & sustainable awqaf and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِذَا مَاتَ الإِنْسَانُ انْقَطَعَ عَنْهُ عَمَلُهُ إِلاَّ مِنْ ثَلاَثَةٍ: صَدَقَةٍ جَارِيَةٍ، أَوْ عِلْمٍ يُنْتَفَعُ بِهِ، أَوْ وَلَدٍ صَالِحٍ يَدْعُو لَهُ
textEnglish: When a human being dies, all his deeds cease except for three: recurring charity (Sadaqah Jariyah), beneficial knowledge left behind, or a righteous child who prays for him.
reference: Sahih Muslim 1631 · Chapter 140: Endowments & Sustainable Awqaf
keyLesson: Invest your life in legacies that continue to shine and generate divine rewards after your earthly departure.

question: How does divine mercy embrace those who strive in endowments & sustainable awqaf and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّمَا الأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ، وَإِنَّمَا لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى
textEnglish: Actions are judged by motives and intentions, and every person will have only that which they intended.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1, Sahih Muslim 1907 · Chapter 140: Endowments & Sustainable Awqaf
keyLesson: Purify your heart before every deed; a sincere intention transforms simple daily acts into perpetual worship.

question: In times of difficulty, how does endowments & sustainable awqaf and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الإِيمَانُ أَنْ تُؤْمِنَ بِاللَّهِ، وَمَلاَئِكَتِهِ، وَكُتُبِهِ، وَرُسُلِهِ، وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ، وَتُؤْمِنَ بِالْقَدَرِ خَيْرِهِ وَشَرِّهِ
textEnglish: Faith is that you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and divine destiny—both its prosperity and adversity.
reference: Sahih Muslim 8 · Chapter 140: Endowments & Sustainable Awqaf
keyLesson: Conviction in Allah’s wisdom gives the believer unwavering calm during life’s unpredictable changes.

question: What reflection on the Hereafter is awakened by endowments & sustainable awqaf and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الرَّاحِمُونَ يَرْحَمُهُمُ الرَّحْمَنُ، ارْحَمُوا مَنْ فِي الأَرْضِ يَرْحَمْكُمْ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاءِ
textEnglish: The merciful will be shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Be merciful to those on earth, and the One in the heavens will be merciful to you.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1924, Sunan Abi Dawud 4941 · Chapter 140: Endowments & Sustainable Awqaf
keyLesson: Compassion to all living beings is the golden key that unlocks divine mercy and forgiveness.

question: How does understanding endowments & sustainable awqaf and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لاَ يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لأَخِيهِ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ
textEnglish: None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 13, Sahih Muslim 45 · Chapter 140: Endowments & Sustainable Awqaf
keyLesson: Genuine faith cleanses the soul of jealousy and cultivates sincere goodwill toward all people.

question: What divine wisdom did the Prophet ﷺ reveal regarding endowments & sustainable awqaf and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّ مِنْ خِيَارِكُمْ أَحْسَنَكُمْ أَخْلاَقًا
textEnglish: Indeed, the best and most beloved among you are those who possess the best character and manners.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 3559, Sahih Muslim 2321 · Chapter 140: Endowments & Sustainable Awqaf
keyLesson: Gentleness, integrity, and warmth of character are the true reflection of a living faith.

question: How does consistent practice of endowments & sustainable awqaf and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الطُّهُورُ شَطْرُ الإِيمَانِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ تَمْلأُ الْمِيزَانَ
textEnglish: Purity is half of faith, and “Alhamdulillah” (Praise be to Allah) fills the divine scale of deeds.
reference: Sahih Muslim 223 · Chapter 140: Endowments & Sustainable Awqaf
keyLesson: Inner and outer purification are intertwined; heartfelt gratitude tilts the eternal scale in your favor.

question: What spiritual remedy does endowments & sustainable awqaf and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: أَوَّلُ مَا يُحَاسَبُ بِهِ الْعَبْدُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ مِنْ عَمَلِهِ صَلاَتُهُ
textEnglish: The first matter for which the slave of Allah will be brought to account on the Day of Judgment is his prayer.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 413, Sunan an-Nasa’i 465 · Chapter 140: Endowments & Sustainable Awqaf
keyLesson: Salah is your personal appointment with the Lord of the worlds; safeguard its punctuality and focus.

question: Why is sincere commitment to endowments & sustainable awqaf and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّ الدِّينَ يُسْرٌ، وَلَنْ يُشَادَّ الدِّينَ أَحَدٌ إِلاَّ غَلَبَهُ
textEnglish: Indeed, the religion is easy, and no one makes the religion overly difficult except that it will overcome him.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 39 · Chapter 140: Endowments & Sustainable Awqaf
keyLesson: Adopt a steady, balanced pace of devotion; moderation sustains lifelong spiritual growth.

question: How did the noble Companions embody endowments & sustainable awqaf and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لَيْسَ الْغِنَى عَنْ كَثْرَةِ الْعَرَضِ، وَلَكِنَّ الْغِنَى غِنَى النَّفْسِ
textEnglish: Richness is not about abundance of worldly possessions; true wealth is the richness of contentment in the soul.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6446, Sahih Muslim 1051 · Chapter 140: Endowments & Sustainable Awqaf
keyLesson: Peace is never found in endless material craving, but in tranquility and satisfaction with what Allah gave.

question: What warning or glad tiding is conveyed concerning endowments & sustainable awqaf and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ فَلْيَقُلْ خَيْرًا أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ
textEnglish: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak what is beneficial or remain silent.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6018, Sahih Muslim 47 · Chapter 140: Endowments & Sustainable Awqaf
keyLesson: Guarding speech protects relationships and preserves the dignity and purity of the heart.

question: In what way does excellence in endowments & sustainable awqaf and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَثَلُ الَّذِي يَذْكُرُ رَبَّهُ وَالَّذِي لاَ يَذْكُرُ رَبَّهُ مَثَلُ الْحَيِّ وَالْمَيِّتِ
textEnglish: The example of the one who remembers his Lord compared to the one who does not is like that of the living and the dead.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6407, Sahih Muslim 779 · Chapter 140: Endowments & Sustainable Awqaf
keyLesson: Dhikr is the oxygen of the spiritual heart; without it, the inner being withers.

question: How can one safeguard endowments & sustainable awqaf and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَا يُصِيبُ الْمُسْلِمَ مِنْ نَصَبٍ وَلاَ وَصَبٍ وَلاَ هَمٍّ وَلاَ حَزَنٍ وَلاَ أَذًى حَتَّى الشَّوْكَةِ يُشَاكُهَا إِلاَّ كَفَّرَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مِنْ خَطَايَاهُ
textEnglish: No fatigue, illness, worry, grief, hurt, or distress befalls a believer—even the prick of a thorn—except that Allah expiates some of his sins through it.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5641, Sahih Muslim 2573 · Chapter 140: Endowments & Sustainable Awqaf
keyLesson: Every silent patience during hardship is recognized, rewarded, and purified by the Most Merciful.

question: What essential principle transforms our approach to endowments & sustainable awqaf and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: تَبَسُّمُكَ فِي وَجْهِ أَخِيكَ لَكَ صَدَقَةٌ
textEnglish: Your smiling in the face of your brother is charity for you.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1956 · Chapter 140: Endowments & Sustainable Awqaf
keyLesson: Radiating warmth and gentle kindness costs nothing yet carries eternal divine reward.

question: Why is genuine devotion in endowments & sustainable awqaf and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الْمُسْلِمُ مَنْ سَلِمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِهِ وَيَدِهِ
textEnglish: The true Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hands other people are completely safe.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 10, Sahih Muslim 40 · Chapter 140: Endowments & Sustainable Awqaf
keyLesson: Righteousness is verified when those around you live in safety from your harm and speech.

question: How does the heart find tranquility through endowments & sustainable awqaf and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
textEnglish: The best among you are those who learn the Quran and teach it to others.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5027 · Chapter 140: Endowments & Sustainable Awqaf
keyLesson: Connecting yourself with the Book of Allah and sharing its light with others is the pinnacle of nobility.

question: What common pitfall did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ warn about in endowments & sustainable awqaf and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ سَلَكَ طَرِيقًا يَلْتَمِسُ فِيهِ عِلْمًا سَهَّلَ اللَّهُ لَهُ بِهِ طَرِيقًا إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ
textEnglish: Whoever travels a path seeking sacred knowledge, Allah makes smooth for him a path to Paradise.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2699 · Chapter 140: Endowments & Sustainable Awqaf
keyLesson: Every moment dedicated to understanding faith and truth brings you closer to the gardens of Jannah.

textArabic: لاَ تَغْضَبْ، فَرَدَّدَ مِرَارًا، قَالَ: لاَ تَغْضَبْ

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6116 · Chapter 140: Endowments & Sustainable Awqaf
keyLesson: Mastery over impulsive anger preserves wisdom, protects relationships, and prevents regret.

question: What eternal reward is promised for cultivating endowments & sustainable awqaf and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?

textEnglish: Be mindful of Allah wherever you are; follow an evil deed with a good one and it will erase it; and treat people with beautiful character.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1987 · Chapter 140: Endowments & Sustainable Awqaf
keyLesson: Live with God-consciousness in private and public, rapidly correct missteps, and be gracious to all.

question: How can parents and mentors inspire endowments & sustainable awqaf and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?

textEnglish: Every one of you is a shepherd and guardian, and every one of you will be questioned concerning his flock.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 893, Sahih Muslim 1829 · Chapter 140: Endowments & Sustainable Awqaf
keyLesson: Leadership is a sacred trust and responsibility of service, not privilege or authority.

question: What guidance did the Prophet ﷺ emphasize regarding consistency in endowments & sustainable awqaf and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ إِذَا عَمِلَ أَحَدُكُمْ عَمَلاً أَنْ يُتْقِنَهُ
textEnglish: Verily, Allah loves that whenever any of you undertakes a work, he executes it with mastery and excellence (Itqan).
reference: Shu’ab al-Iman (Al-Bayhaqi 4929, Hasan) · Chapter 140: Endowments & Sustainable Awqaf
keyLesson: Excellence in profession, study, and daily duty is an act of devotion loved by the Creator.

question: How does divine mercy embrace those who strive in endowments & sustainable awqaf and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الْحَيَاءُ لاَ يَأْتِي إِلاَّ بِخَيْرٍ
textEnglish: Modesty and conscience (Haya) bring nothing except goodness.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6117, Sahih Muslim 37 · Chapter 140: Endowments & Sustainable Awqaf
keyLesson: Haya is a spiritual shield that restrains the soul from vulgarity and prompts noble conduct.

question: In times of difficulty, how does endowments & sustainable awqaf and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ كَفَلَ يَتِيمًا لَهُ أَوْ لِغَيْرِهِ فَأَنَا وَهُوَ كَهَاتَيْنِ فِي الْجَنَّةِ

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5304, Sahih Muslim 2983 · Chapter 140: Endowments & Sustainable Awqaf
keyLesson: Caring for vulnerable orphans guarantees the closest companionship with the Prophet ﷺ in the highest Jannah.

question: What warning or glad tiding is conveyed concerning endowments & sustainable awqaf and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِذَا مَاتَ الإِنْسَانُ انْقَطَعَ عَنْهُ عَمَلُهُ إِلاَّ مِنْ ثَلاَثَةٍ: صَدَقَةٍ جَارِيَةٍ، أَوْ عِلْمٍ يُنْتَفَعُ بِهِ، أَوْ وَلَدٍ صَالِحٍ يَدْعُو لَهُ
textEnglish: When a human being dies, all his deeds cease except for three: recurring charity (Sadaqah Jariyah), beneficial knowledge left behind, or a righteous child who prays for him.
reference: Sahih Muslim 1631 · Chapter 140: Endowments & Sustainable Awqaf
keyLesson: Invest your life in legacies that continue to shine and generate divine rewards after your earthly departure.

question: In what way does excellence in endowments & sustainable awqaf and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: إِنَّمَا الأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ، وَإِنَّمَا لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى
textEnglish: Actions are judged by motives and intentions, and every person will have only that which they intended.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1, Sahih Muslim 1907 · Chapter 140: Endowments & Sustainable Awqaf
keyLesson: Purify your heart before every deed; a sincere intention transforms simple daily acts into perpetual worship.

question: How can one safeguard endowments & sustainable awqaf and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الإِيمَانُ أَنْ تُؤْمِنَ بِاللَّهِ، وَمَلاَئِكَتِهِ، وَكُتُبِهِ، وَرُسُلِهِ، وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ، وَتُؤْمِنَ بِالْقَدَرِ خَيْرِهِ وَشَرِّهِ
textEnglish: Faith is that you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and divine destiny—both its prosperity and adversity.
reference: Sahih Muslim 8 · Chapter 140: Endowments & Sustainable Awqaf
keyLesson: Conviction in Allah’s wisdom gives the believer unwavering calm during life’s unpredictable changes.

question: What essential principle transforms our approach to endowments & sustainable awqaf and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الرَّاحِمُونَ يَرْحَمُهُمُ الرَّحْمَنُ، ارْحَمُوا مَنْ فِي الأَرْضِ يَرْحَمْكُمْ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاءِ
textEnglish: The merciful will be shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Be merciful to those on earth, and the One in the heavens will be merciful to you.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1924, Sunan Abi Dawud 4941 · Chapter 140: Endowments & Sustainable Awqaf
keyLesson: Compassion to all living beings is the golden key that unlocks divine mercy and forgiveness.

question: Why is genuine devotion in endowments & sustainable awqaf and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لاَ يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لأَخِيهِ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ
textEnglish: None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 13, Sahih Muslim 45 · Chapter 140: Endowments & Sustainable Awqaf
keyLesson: Genuine faith cleanses the soul of jealousy and cultivates sincere goodwill toward all people.

question: What spiritual wisdom did the Prophet ﷺ teach regarding contentment with moderate earnings (qana’ah)?
textArabic: الْحَيَاءُ لاَ يَأْتِي إِلاَّ بِخَيْرٍ
textEnglish: Modesty and conscience (Haya) bring nothing except goodness.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6117, Sahih Muslim 37 · Chapter 141: Contentment with Moderate Earnings (Qana’ah)
keyLesson: Haya is a spiritual shield that restrains the soul from vulgarity and prompts noble conduct.

question: What divine wisdom did the Prophet ﷺ reveal regarding contentment with moderate earnings (qana’ah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ كَفَلَ يَتِيمًا لَهُ أَوْ لِغَيْرِهِ فَأَنَا وَهُوَ كَهَاتَيْنِ فِي الْجَنَّةِ
textEnglish: The one who cares for an orphan and myself will be together in Paradise like these two fingers (joining his index and middle finger).
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5304, Sahih Muslim 2983 · Chapter 141: Contentment with Moderate Earnings (Qana’ah)
keyLesson: Caring for vulnerable orphans guarantees the closest companionship with the Prophet ﷺ in the highest Jannah.

question: How does consistent practice of contentment with moderate earnings (qana’ah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَا نَقَصَتْ صَدَقَةٌ مِنْ مَالٍ، وَمَا زَادَ اللَّهُ عَبْدًا بِعَفْوٍ إِلاَّ عِزًّا
textEnglish: Charity never decreases wealth; and Allah never increases a servant who forgives except in honor and elevation.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2588 · Chapter 141: Contentment with Moderate Earnings (Qana’ah)
keyLesson: Generosity and forgiveness never degrade a person; they invoke divine barakah and nobility.

question: What spiritual remedy does contentment with moderate earnings (qana’ah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: احْفَظِ اللَّهَ يَحْفَظْكَ، احْفَظِ اللَّهَ تَجِدْهُ تُجَاهَكَ
textEnglish: Be mindful of Allah, and He will protect you. Be mindful of Allah, and you will find Him facing you in every need.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2516 · Chapter 141: Contentment with Moderate Earnings (Qana’ah)
keyLesson: Honor Allah’s commands in times of ease, and He will deliver and comfort you in times of adversity.

question: Why is sincere commitment to contentment with moderate earnings (qana’ah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: لَوْ أَنَّكُمْ تَوَكَّلُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ حَقَّ تَوَكُّلِهِ لَرَزَقَكُمْ كَمَا يَرْزُقُ الطَّيْرَ
textEnglish: If you were to rely upon Allah with true reliance (Tawakkul), He would provide for you just as He provides for birds: they depart hungry at dawn and return full at dusk.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2344, Sunan Ibn Majah 4164 · Chapter 141: Contentment with Moderate Earnings (Qana’ah)
keyLesson: Combine practical effort with tranquil reliance upon the Ultimate Provider.

question: How did the noble Companions embody contentment with moderate earnings (qana’ah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: أَفْشُوا السَّلاَمَ، وَأَطْعِمُوا الطَّعَامَ، وَصِلُوا الأَرْحَامَ، وَصَلُّوا بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّاسُ نِيَامٌ، تَدْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ بِسَلاَمٍ
textEnglish: Spread peace (Salam), feed the hungry, maintain kinship ties, and pray during the night while people sleep: you will enter Paradise in complete peace.
reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2485, Sunan Ibn Majah 3251 · Chapter 141: Contentment with Moderate Earnings (Qana’ah)
keyLesson: The four golden keys to peaceful entry into Jannah unite communal kindness and private devotion.

question: What warning or glad tiding is conveyed concerning contentment with moderate earnings (qana’ah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الصَّدَقَةُ تَقَعُ فِي يَدِ الرَّحْمَنِ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَقَعَ فِي يَدِ السَّائِلِ
textEnglish: Charity falls into the Hand of the Most Merciful before it falls into the hand of the needy person.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1410, Sahih Muslim 1014 · Chapter 141: Contentment with Moderate Earnings (Qana’ah)
keyLesson: Give charity with profound reverence; you are offering a direct transaction with your Lord.

question: In what way does excellence in contentment with moderate earnings (qana’ah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: الْمُؤْمِنُ الْقَوِيُّ خَيْرٌ وَأَحَبُّ إِلَى اللَّهِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِ الضَّعِيفِ، وَفِي كُلٍّ خَيْرٌ
textEnglish: The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, though there is goodness in both. Strive for what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not lose heart.
reference: Sahih Muslim 2664 · Chapter 141: Contentment with Moderate Earnings (Qana’ah)
keyLesson: Cultivate mental, moral, physical, and spiritual strength while maintaining humble reliance on Allah.

question: How can one safeguard contentment with moderate earnings (qana’ah) and how does it elevate a believer’s character and relationship with Allah?
textArabic: مَنْ سَرَّهُ أَنْ يُبْسَطَ لَهُ فِي رِزْقِهِ، وَأَنْ يُنْسَأَ لَهُ فِي أَثَرِهِ، فَلْيَصِلْ رَحِمَهُ
textEnglish: Whoever delights in having his provision expanded and his lifespan blessed and extended, let him maintain ties of kinship.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5986, Sahih Muslim 2557 · Chapter 141: Contentment with Moderate Earnings (Qana’ah)
keyLesson: Kindness to relatives and family reconciliation draws barakah into time and livelihood.

textArabic: إِذَا مَاتَ الإِنْسَانُ انْقَطَعَ عَنْهُ عَمَلُهُ إِلاَّ مِنْ ثَلاَثَةٍ: صَدَقَةٍ جَارِيَةٍ، أَوْ عِلْمٍ يُنْتَفَعُ بِهِ، أَوْ وَلَدٍ صَالِحٍ يَدْعُو لَهُ
textEnglish: When a human being dies, all his deeds cease except for three: recurring charity (Sadaqah Jariyah), beneficial knowledge left behind, or a righteous child who prays for him.
